This role is based in Costa Mesa, CA, and supports Anduril’s manufacturing operations, including sites at Quonset Point, RI and Atlanta, GA; specific team, site, and program assignments are determined during the interview process based on business need and candidate background.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Lead formal machine and task-based risk assessments on production equipment, fixtures, tooling, and processes, documenting hazards, risk ratings, required controls, and residual risk.
  • Review manufacturing work instructions and supporting training material for safety adequacy; author Job Hazard Analyses (JHA) and embed the required controls, PPE, and safe-work steps.
  • Engineer and review production equipment such as lift fixtures and material-handling aids in partnership with EHS, and support proof-load testing.
  • Assess and design safety into production test equipment.
  • Apply the hierarchy of controls and prevention-through-design principles to eliminate or reduce hazards at the equipment and line-design stage.
  • Define functional-safety requirements for safety-related control systems and verify their implementation.
  • Partner with EHS to ensure engineering controls satisfy applicable OSHA 29 CFR 1910 general-industry requirements (machine guarding, lockout/tagout, electrical, PPE, materials handling).
  • Support incident and near-miss investigations and root-cause analysis; drive corrective engineering actions and management of change.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • B.S. Degree in Mechanical, Electrical, Manufacturing, Industrial, or Safety Engineering, or equivalent technical discipline
  • 7+ years of experience in manufacturing/machine safety, equipment or controls engineering, or a related discipline with demonstrated ownership of risk assessments
  • Hands-on experience performing formal machine and task-based risk assessments and applying the hierarchy of controls
  • Working knowledge of machine safeguarding and applicable OSHA 29 CFR 1910 general-industry requirements, including machine guarding and the control of hazardous energy (lockout/tagout)
  • Experience developing Job Hazard Analyses (JHA) and translating risk-assessment findings into work instructions, controls, and training
  • Experience designing safety into production and/or test equipment, partnering with EHS and electrical safety specialists
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence cross-functionally on the factory floor and with engineering teams
  • Eligibility to pursue and maintain a U.S. security clearance, as required

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Familiarity with machine safety standards such as ISO 12100 (risk assessment and risk reduction), ISO 13849 (safety-related parts of control systems), and ANSI B11 (machine safety and safeguarding)
  • M.S. Degree in an engineering discipline, or a professional safety credential (CSP, ASP) or machinery-safety credential (CMSE)
  • Functional-safety experience determining Performance Level or SIL for safety-related control systems, and functional-safety certification (CMSE or TÜV FSEng)
  • Experience with production test-equipment safety
  • Experience in a high-rate or rapidly scaling manufacturing environment, ideally in aerospace, defense, automotive, or a comparable regulated industry
  • Active U.S. security clearance

As a System Safety Engineer at Anduril, you will autonomously drive system-level safety decisions, apply advanced analysis techniques, influence design trades, and lead complex failure investigations.   • Develop safety requirements and collaborate with design teams to implement safety solutions
  • Identify and document hazards and risks, manage hazard tracking, and ensure proper risk mitigation strategies are in place
  • Support the Design Requirements Process to ensure teams adhere to safety best practices
  • Support Development Milestone Reviews (PDR, CDR, QDR) representing System Safety
  • Lead Safety corrective actions from RCCA investigations and Mishap Reports
  • Verify and validate risk and hazard reduction measures
  • Liaise with internal stakeholders and support customer and regulatory engagements as needed
  • Drive continuous improvement in System Safety processes and methodologies
  • Ensure compliance with relevant military and industry safety standards

  • Minimum of 5 years of industry experience as a System Safety Engineer or equivalent engineering background
  • B.S. degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Systems Engineering, or equivalent technical discipline
  • Experience with safety-critical hardware and software systems in the defense or aerospace industry
  • Familiarity with MIL-STD-882E and other relevant safety standards
  • Strong background in safety analysis techniques including FTA, FHA, SCFTA, and FMECA
  • Experience with requirements decomposition for Safety
  • Failure investigation/analysis experience with a proven track record of solving problems and preventing reoccurrence
  • Design Review experience (PDR, CDR, MRR) and confident presentation skills
  • Strong analytical/problem-solving skills and excellent communication skills with the ability to collaborate cross-functionally

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Mission Success team is a cross-functional group that partners with every business line and supports all products that Anduril builds. Our responsibilities include product operations, training and adoption, and user documentation. We are seeking an experienced Technical Writer to create and maintain user documentation across our diverse business lines. We believe that the quality of our documentation should reflect the quality of our products, which are world-class.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Technical Writer, your mission is to partner with our numerous product and operations teams to deliver accurate, updated, and easy-to-understand documentation on how to use Anduril products. You will do whatever it takes to organize our engineering and program delivery functions in this mission. In this role, you will work closely with engineers, operations, and various subject matter experts to understand our products, identify user workflows, and use documentation to close the gap. As such, the Technical Writer will play a foundational role in setting the bar for tone, voice, and quality across our written artifacts. 

With Anduril’s focus on defense and national security, user documentation plays a critical role in ensuring front-line operators know how to leverage the “arsenal of democracy.” Your mission is to make the process of learning how to operate complex hardware and software systems as easy and seamless as possible, with exceptionally well-written and presented artifacts. 

You will identify relevant stakeholders and lead them through a documentation roadmap with established key milestones and targets. You will engage subject matter experts at the right time, and you will guide them towards a finished user-facing document that plainly meets customer needs. Finally, you will work with our account teams to ensure that contract deliverables are accurate, on-time, and in the right format. 

Written content artifacts under this charter may include things like: technical manuals, operational manuals, maintenance manuals, procedures, checklists, templates, user guides, troubleshooting guides, and release notes. You will partner with account, product, and engineering teams across all phases of product development to ensure users have the right documentation available. 

Along with our commercial offerings outlined above, Anduril is pursuing Programs with the GOV, which require documentation in standards such as MIL-STD-40051D and S1000D, delivered via IETMs / IETDs. Familiarity with these standards and delivery methods is highly desired. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Generate, review, and edit documentation that is user-focused. Work with engineering and operations to deliver task, conditions, and standard-centric documentation.
  • Evaluate and prioritize tasks required to successfully support product documentation efforts and keep them on track. Help drive the best decision for the company by using a data-driven approach and considering input from stakeholders to ensure well-informed decisions.
  • Communicate and help manage expectations. Ensure risks are noted with adequate time and shared with leadership.
  • Help build a culture of technical documentation by contributing to the living documentation process, ensuring that those who come after you learn from your acquired Anduril experience.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years of demonstrated excellence generating technical documentation for complex hardware, software, or aerospace systems.
  • Experience writing technical, user-facing documentation.
  • Experience reading and interpreting engineering documentation (e.g., schematics, CAD, or software specs).
  • Experience building content in a variety of formats (Word, XML, DITA, etc.).
  • Strong written/verbal communication and interpersonal skills, with an emphasis on explaining highly technical subjects simply.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. security clearance.
  • Ability to relocate, if not already local, to be onsite in Costa Mesa, CA.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Military exposure and experience, particularly with military technical documentation writing and formatting standards, guidelines, and verbiage (MIL-STD-40051, S1000D, etc.).
  • Passion for excellent documentation and user experience.
  • Previous experience creating technical documentation in Aerospace and Defense (for DoD).
  • Experience delivering content on fast-paced, complex projects with multiple stakeholders.

As Scale AI continues its historic growth trajectory in Generative AI, we are seeking a Growth Strategy & Operations Lead to help ensure our customer projects have the expert capacity they need to deliver on time. Growth at Scale is not traditional user acquisition: our team manages the supply side of Outlier, Scale’s expert contributor marketplace, sourcing, onboarding, activating, retaining, and routing highly skilled contributors such as PhDs, coders, and domain experts to the AI projects that need them most.

This demanding and multi-faceted role requires a unique blend of strategy, operations, and analytics. You will work across acquisition channels, onboarding and screening funnels, contributor training, retention programs, and project ramp planning to build the expert supply engine behind Scale’s most strategic Generative AI work.

You will:

  • Drive critical growth projects that expand and improve the expert supply available for Scale’s highest-priority AI projects, collaborating closely with Engineering, Operations, Go-to-Market, and project delivery teams.

  • Improve onboarding, screening, verification, and training systems so that experts can be evaluated, activated, and ramped onto customer projects quickly and reliably.

  • Strong technical background (a degree in STEM is ideal, and at minimum the role requires the ability to do data analytics using SQL or Python).

Job Description:

Lead the future of physical AI in defense by building the reasoning models for unmanned autonomous systems, across aerial, maritime, land, and space domains. 

We are looking for a leader with not only the deep technical expertise or the abilities to build a world-class team, but also someone with the strong conviction that AI will protect service members and civilians. This role is responsible for building and leading a team that researches and designs models, establishes training pipelines and rigorous evaluations, and ensures mission effectiveness at the edge under real-world constraints. These models must support individual vehicles and coordinated teams of hundreds of agents, while meeting the constraints of operating at the edge in contested environments. 

In this role, you’ll partner closely with world-class teams in perception, MLOps, large-scale simulation, and inference to deliver capabilities as part of the broader Hivemind Enterprise team. 

What success looks like: your team’s reasoning models deliver exceptional outcomes for baseline platforms and missions, which can then be rapidly and confidently adapted to new platforms and missions by our solutions engineering organisation. 

What you'll do:

  • Build & lead the team that designs, trains, adapts, and evaluates reasoning and cognition models intended for deployment across our unmanned platforms. 
  • Define the technical roadmap for single-agent and multi-agent models, including architecture choices, training methods, data strategy, and evaluation criteria. 
  • Make informed tradeoffs among foundation-model approaches (e.g. VLMs, VLAs), specialized deep-learning models, and traditional AI/ML methods. 
  • Advance model capabilities for interpreting context, reasoning over time, coordinating among agents, and adapting to incomplete or changing information. 
  • Drive training efforts, including appropriate use of self-supervised learning, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and distillation. 
  • Establish rigorous evaluations in simulation and with real-world data. Measure generalization, robustness, uncertainty, and performance as team size and operating conditions change. 
  • Recruit, develop, and manage a high-performing team of AI/ML engineers. 
  • Translate edge constraints into model-design and training decisions in partnership with hardware, autonomy, and inference teams. 
  • Communicate technical tradeoffs and model limitations clearly to research, engineering, product, and organizational leadership. 
  • Deliver trained models and clear performance evidence to partner teams. 
  • Create tight feedback loops among model failures, data curation, training experiments, and re-evaluation. 

Required qualifications:

  • BS/MS in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, and/or similar degree, or equivalent practical experience. Typically requires a minimum of 10 years of related experience with a Bachelor’s degree; or 9 years and a Master’s degree; or 8 years with a PhD; or equivalent work experience. 
  • Exceptional track record of leading the development and deployment of state-of-the-art ML models in production environments, making difficult prioritisation decisions, and communicating tradeoffs across disciplines. 
  • 5+ years of people management experience leading engineering or applied research teams, with demonstrated success hiring, coaching, developing technical leaders, and managing performance. 
  • Deep expertise in foundation models, modern deep learning, model architectures, and the training ecosystem. 
  • Strong command of training and adaptation approaches such as self-supervised learning, supervised fine-tuning, imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and distillation. 
  • Experience defining datasets, training objectives, experimental workflows, benchmarks, and reproducible criteria for comparing models. 
  • Fluency in traditional AI/ML techniques and an ability to combine them thoughtfully with learned models. 
  • Experience with training frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, TensorFlow, etc. 
  • Experience with multimodal, embodied, robotic, or autonomous-system models; familiarity with VLA models and world models is particularly relevant. 
  • Strong familiarity with traditional robotics algorithms, e.g. path planning, probabilistic modeling, optimization approaches, etc. 
  • Familiarity with NVIDIA Jetson and other edge compute platforms (e.g. Qualcomm, AMD, etc.) 

Preferred qualifications:

  • PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or similar degree. 
  • Expertise in optimising and deploying ML models to resource-constrained hardware platforms. 
  • Experience with simulation-to-real on autonomous systems. 
  • Experience managing managers or leading multiple engineering teams. 
  • Experience with unmanned autonomous systems in defense applications 
  • Familiarity with large, distributed systems 
  • Familiarity with high-fidelity simulation, e.g. rigid body dynamics, sensor & actuator models, etc. 
  • Experience managing and interfacing with external partners and vendors

There's no such thing as a "safe system" - only safer systems. Our Security team works to create and maintain the safest operating environment for Google's users and developers. As a Security Engineer, you help protect network boundaries, keep computer systems and network devices hardened against attacks and provide security services to protect highly sensitive data like passwords and customer information. Security Engineers work directly with network equipment and actively monitor our systems for attacks and intrusions. You also work with software engineers to proactively identify and fix security flaws and vulnerabilities.

You use your industry experience to own and drive the resolution of complex security incidents, policy questions and technical security issues.

SPMA (Security and Privacy for Mergers, Acquisitions and Alphabet) team’s mandate is focused on reducing Acquisitions, third-party and Cloud risk to Google and Alphabet.

SPMA executes on its mandate through three key verticals:

  • Mergers, Acquisitions and Alphabets (M&A): Effectively and safely raise the security bar for Google’s Off Google entities (Acquisitions and Bets); helping companies navigate Google’s security landscape and processes, thereby safely and securely integrating/divesting/separating them.
  • Alphabet Use of Cloud (AUC): Manage and minimize risk from Alphabet’s use of public clouds (GCP).
  • Third-party/Vendor Security Diligence (3PSD): Ensure effective governance and minimize risk from Alphabet’s use of third-party vendors.
This role sits within the Third Party/Vendor Security Diligence (3PSD) vertical, focusing on third-party security. Alphabet’s Third Party Security Diligence program ensures security of our third-party engagements, and is part of a broader third-party risk management ecosystem.

The Core team builds the technical foundation behind Google’s flagship products. We are owners and advocates for the underlying design elements, developer platforms, product components, and infrastructure at Google. These are the essential building blocks for excellent, safe, and coherent experiences for our users and drive the pace of innovation for every developer. We look across Google’s products to build central solutions, break down technical barriers and strengthen existing systems. As the Core team, we have a mandate and a unique opportunity to impact important technical decisions across the company.

Researchers in artificial intelligence (AI) are building systems that can reason, plan and act on behalf of the people who use them, from writing software to automating complex, multistep tasks. As these systems become more capable and more widely used, making them efficient matters more and more. That means getting the most value from the compute they use, choosing the right capabilities for each task, and adapting to the needs of the people and environments they serve.

 

Microsoft's deep investments in the field are advancing the state of the art in efficient and agentic AI. Its researchers combine machine learning, systems research and rigorous empirical evaluation to understand how intelligent systems can balance quality, speed and cost, and how they can improve with experience. The research, tools and services that result are woven into existing and new products and, at the same time, made open and accessible to the broader community in a bid to accelerate innovation, democratize AI and help developers and organizations do more with the resources they have.



Responsibilities

Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Research internships are available in all areas of research, and are offered year-round, though they typically begin in the summer.

Required Qualifications

Other Requirements

  • Research Interns are expected to be physically located in their manager’s Microsoft worksite location for the duration of their internship.

  • Experience conducting research on the efficiency, cost, or performance of machine learning models or systems (e.g., inference optimization, model selection, model compression, or adaptive computation).

This work involves transitioning business-critical data and traffic to modern systems without disrupting existing services or customers. Overview

Microsoft Frontier Company is redefining how enterprises transform — bringing agentic AI, cloud-scale computing, data, simulation, and human expertise together so customers turn ambition into measurable business impact. As customers look to reinvent how work gets done — redesigning business processes, operating models, and human-agent ways of working across industries and functions — they need more than a platform. They need experts who can understand their business outcomes, reinvent new ways of working, and enable their employees to adopt that change at speed.  

The AI Workforce Reinvention Architect will be the specialist  on the ground with customers developing the new ways of working, deploying agents and AI to enable and reinforce those patterns, and empower customers to own the behavioral transformation as they evolve from AI experimentation to AI-native operations. In this role, you will own the end-to-end operations reinvention with the end results being a continuous, always-on cycle rather than a one-off program. You will embed AI-first ways of working into culture, processes, and performance systems, working directly with business, technology and HR leaders, along with Microsoft account teams, industry specialists, and engineers.  

This is a role for people who do the higher-judgment human work that technology can inform but not perform. You will help customer reimage how people and agents work together – while shaping repeatable patterns specific to industries and functions. If you’re energized by making change stick rather than launching programs that fade, this role is for you.  

In this role you bring a unique blend of technical, industry, and change management expertise. Your edge is translating a customer’s business outcomes into a tangible operating model, powered by agents, with a clear path for adoption. Customers feel confident investing in frontier transformation because they see a viable plan for their teams to transform in parallel.  

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.   



Responsibilities

Workforce Reinvention 

  • Define new ways of working and employee roles based on the customer’s industry, function, and business outcomes/KPIs 

  • Design and deploy agents and AI systems that empower and scale employees and teams to execute 

  • Deliver retraining programmes ensuring no employee is left behind 

  • Embed AI adoption into performance evaluations and onboarding processes 

  • Protect employee privacy to maintain trust and stay on the right side of regulations  

Strategic Change Leadership 

  • Design and execute comprehensive operating model changes powered by AI with enterprise scale, structured as a continuous, always-on cycle rather than a fixed, one-off sequence 

  • Conduct AI/Agent readiness assessments to identify organisational barriers and enablers 

  • Develop AI literacy plans that position AI and agents as new ways of working, not tools 

  • Establish and lead AI Council and Champion networks to drive grassroots adoption through the informal networks of trusted peers 

Adoption Programme Delivery 

  • Implement a structured adoption framework powered by workplace adoption analytics and role-based enablement 

  • Coordinate communications, training, and champion efforts across thousands of users 

  • Drive behavioural change by creating recognition rather than pushing content at them 

  • Scale training globally: live sessions, on-demand tutorials, internal support communities 

Stakeholder Engagement 

  • Facilitate business and technology leadership workshops and roundtables to design for required impact and scale  

  • Ensure cross-functional collaboration across IT, HR, operations, and business unit leadership on how work will change and their hands-on role  

  • Build trust through responsible experimentation and transparent communication 

  • Monitor usage statistics and qualitative feedback, adjusting programmes to maintain momentum, and measure success by whether change persists at 90, 180, and 360 days  



Qualifications

Required/minimum qualifications 

  • Master's OR Bachelor’s Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or related field AND several years of experience in technology solutions, practice development, architecture, consulting, and/or technology domain (e.g., Security) OR equivalent experience. 

  • Solid experience in  managing multiple projects or portfolios. 

  • Experience leading blended, multidisciplinary teams. 

Additional or preferred qualifications 

  • Solid experience in managing cross-functional teams  

  • Demonstrated success leading change programmes across 5,000+ user populations 

  • Experience with AI/ML adoption programmes or digital transformation initiatives 

  • Understanding of Microsoft 365 Copilot, AI agents, and agentic workflow concepts 

  • Hands-on AI fluency — confident enough to build alongside the tools, interpret the data they produce, and understand their limits

As a member of the Battery Modeling team, you will be responsible for Thermal performance modeling of battery systems for all Apple products. You will be closely integrated with the Battery Module, Product teams, Battery Modeling and Cell Engineering from the early design stages, analyzing and informing the design of cutting-edge products. You will own evaluation and quality assurance for every layer of the product — from whether the system is being correctly triggered for the right set of user requests, through whether it surfaces and ranks the right results, to whether the underlying transactions execute correctly, including integrations with external partner APIs, and financial systems. correctness, all against a large, constantly evolving real-world dataset.

Catching and preventing quality regressions across an entire product surface — from user-facing correctness to backend transaction integrity.

We are looking for a Data Center Central Planning Manager () to join Meta’s Data Center Strategic Planning organization. In this role, you will drive the development of constraint-aware data center capacity plans that translate product growth, AI workload evolution, and fleet architecture into actionable roadmaps across power (MW), cooling, space, and network. You will work at the intersection of capacity engineering, portfolio planning, and investment decisioning, building quantitative analyses and scenarios that inform major infrastructure choices. You’ll be expected to go deep in the data and engineering constraints, partner effectively across Capacity Engineering, Facilities, Network, Construction, Site Selection, Finance, and Operations, and communicate clear recommendations that move decisions forward.

Responsibilities

  • Drive portfolio capacity plans connecting demand signals (product + AI) to supply plans and execution paths across MW delivery, cooling envelope, space readiness, and network capacity, including near-to-mid term roadmaps and readiness milestones
  • Build and maintain quantitative planning models (supply/demand, scenario analysis, sensitivities, bottleneck identification, schedule-risk and uncertainty modeling) to support prioritization and sequencing decisions
  • Translate workload characteristics (GPU/AI clusters, rack power density, resiliency tiers, topology/interconnect needs, placement constraints) into facility and electrical requirements, including megawatt ramp profiles, readiness gates, and deployment constraints
  • Assess system-level constraints across fleet and pipeline (utility delivery, substation/transformer capacity, cooling limits, heat rejection, building envelopes, network ingress/egress, construction sequencing) and drive mitigation plans in partnership with directly responsible teams
  • Develop decision packages and narratives: synthesize analyses into clear trade-offs and recommendations (cost, schedule, reliability, operability, risk), explicitly calling out assumptions and sensitivities
  • Partner with senior stakeholders by aligning pre-reads, surfacing key risks early, and supporting decision-making in planning forums—maintaining strong technical credibility with engineering partners
  • Drive cross-functional execution: align dependencies, track closure of gaps, manage escalations as needed, and support planning governance (cadence, documentation, model hygiene)

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Applied Math, Physics, Operations Research, or equivalent practical experience

  • Demonstrated ability to lead ambiguous, cross-functional problems to decision and execution; ability to create structure and drive progress through partners
  • Strong quantitative background: experience building models, performing scenario and sensitivity analysis, and making recommendations under uncertainty
  • Technical fluency across data center domains is sufficient to drive trade-offs and identify bottlenecks (power systems, cooling, facility constraints, and network capacity)

  • Hands-on capability with Python and SQL (or equivalent tooling) to build reproducible analysis and planning models

About the Role

We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join our Beneficial Deployments, Life Sciences team. This is a partner-facing role: you'll support nonprofits, research institutes, academic medical centres and public-sector funders as they use Claude to get treatments to patients with rare and neglected diseases, where there is little or no commercial incentive to fund development.

The role focuses on clinical development, where we think Claude can help these partners today. Trials in these diseases have small patient populations, investigator-led or nonprofit funding and little operational support, and they often stall on protocol quality, operational risk and site start-up. Claude can help teams design better trials and start them sooner. Much of this work is drug repurposing: testing new uses for approved, usually off-patent or generic medicines, whose known safety profiles can let a good hypothesis reach patients years sooner than a new molecule.

You'll advise and embed in partners' teams, building alongside their engineers, scientists and clinicians.

  • Work with partners' trial teams to design, review and prioritise clinical trials with Claude: drafting and reviewing protocols and statistical analysis plans, and flagging enrolment and operational risks.

  • Build reusable infrastructure other institutions can adopt (MCP servers for biomedical data sources, agent skills, benchmarks grounded in real clinical questions), and feed what you learn in the field back to product, engineering and research.

  • Hands-on clinical development experience: designing, running or analysing clinical trials, or assessing clinical evidence to decide which programmes go forward (for example due diligence or asset evaluation).   • Comfort with biomedical data: literature, omics, and real-world patient data (health records, registries, claims), ideally inside secure or trusted research environments.

This role sits at the centre of how Dive-XL's software capabilities are shaped and delivered. You will work closely with stakeholders across Dive-XL Platform engineering, Maritime Enabling Technology, Maritime Application Development, and Program teams to drive product design, particularly around the software features delivered on the mission software layer. If you want to own the "what" and the "why" for software on a platform that is actively deployed and scaling, this is the role.

About the Job

Software Product Managers develop a detailed understanding of user, customer, and business needs, define what to build, why to build it, then independently lead projects to integrate those software capabilities with our products. This includes autonomy, simulation, data processing, payload integration, and off-board command and control or decision support. We expect Software Product Managers to demonstrate end-to-end outcome ownership of one or more significant projects or products, driving work through our engineering governance process, co-ordinating and directly contributing to project execution, and managing adoption of the solution by internal and external customers. Our Software Product Managers will also provide tactical subject matter expertise to cross-functional engineering teams as required.

  • Be an expert on the existing and future planned product capabilities for your products

  • Manage a 6 - 18 month roadmap for your allocated projects
  • Define, document, gain consensus for, and communicate appropriate goals and plans for your projects, derived from broader organizational vision, strategy, and priorities
  • Co-ordinate your project(s) roadmap and execution with other teams across Anduril, with the aim of developing components that are re-usable across multiple Anduril product lines
  • Be responsible for co-ordinating and directly contributing to execution on one or more Software Engineering projects from definition through to delivery, optimizing for the delivery of value to the end-user
  • Drive work through Anduril’s engineering governance process, working with your teams to present plans and designs to internal stakeholders
  • Manage programmatic risk for your projects, and collaborate with engineers to manage technical risk, including sound and timely decision making
  • Work as a leader of multi-disciplinary project teams of 4 - 10 members across team boundaries
  • Collaborate with internal and external customer teams to drive adoption of your delivered software solutions
  • Travel to co-locate with end-users and/or other teams up to 20% of the time

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Robotics, Mechatronics, Computer Science, Engineering, a relevant field, or equivalent experience
  • Extensive professional experience working as a Software Product Manager with one or more domains of expertise
  • Capacity to act as the owner for a software system, including stakeholder engagement, requirements definition, roadmap management, team co-ordination, design, implementation management, sustainment and evolution
  • Capacity to learn and grow individually, while mentoring junior team members effectively, building team cohesion and capacity
  • Experience leading the design and execution of user engagement and research studies
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an Australian Government security clearance

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in the delivery or employment of a military mission system and/or autonomous vehicle
  • Experience with the design, implementation and operation of horizontally scaled cloud technologies
  • Experience with the design, implementation and support of embedded software, particularly in the field of robotics
  • Experience with the design, implementation, roll-out, and evolution of user-facing front-end applications
  • Experience with the development of high assurance safety critical software, including with DO-178, IEC 61508, or similar standards
  • Experience with the development of modeling and simulation capabilities
  • Desire to learn and grow into other roles that require experience as a Senior Software Product Manager, such as Staff Software Product Manager

Job Description:

As a Staff or Senior Staff Landing Gear Engineer, you will take full technical ownership of the landing gear architecture, kinematic mechanism design, structural analysis, and vehicle integration for a new UAV platform. Serving as the sole landing gear subject matter expert on this program, you will work from first principles to execute mechanism trades, perform structural hand calculations, design hardware, manage external component suppliers, support proposals and capture, and deliver flight-ready systems in a rapid-iteration development environment. This position requires a balance of technical rigor, rapid decision-making, and hands-on engineering to efficiently transition concepts into operational capability. The ideal candidate is comfortable solving complex problems, taking ownership, working within an accelerated aircraft development environment, and is motivated by getting meaningful capability into the hands of operators quickly. 

What you'll do:

  • Architecture and Kinematic Trades: Lead landing gear architecture definition and trade studies (e.g., electro-mechanical vs. hydro-mechanical actuation, fixed vs. retractable kinematics, stowage packaging) to meet vehicle mass, volume, and ground ground handling requirements. 
  • Mechanism and Structural Design: Own the full CAD design lifecycle from initial concept through drawing release, including complex linkage kinematics, clearance envelopes, structural load paths, material selection, and rigorous tolerance stack-ups. 
  • Structural and Dynamic Sizing: Perform first-principles classical stress and fatigue hand calculations, backed by finite element analysis (linear/non-linear, modal, buckling) and dynamic landing load assessments. 
  • Subsystem Sizing and Selection: Size and select wheels, tires, brakes, shock absorption systems, actuators, and nose wheel steering mechanisms tailored to vehicle landing and taxi envelopes.
  • Component Sourcing and Vendor Management: Author technical specifications and statements of work (SOW) for landing gear components, evaluate vendors, and drive supplier technical execution. 
  • Test, Drop Qualification, and Validation: Define verification test plans, design mechanical test fixtures, support drop test campaigns, and execute functional validation against performance requirements. 
  • Integration and Flight Test Support: Support prototype assembly, ground taxi testing, and flight test operations to identify discrepancies, resolve mechanism anomalies via root-cause investigation, and implement rapid design changes. 

Required qualifications:

  • Experience: minimum 7 years (L4) to 12 years (L5) of direct experience in aerospace mechanism design, aircraft landing gear systems, or primary structural development.
  • Education: B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Core Fundamentals: Deep mastery of classical solid mechanics, kinematics, dynamics, fatigue, materials selection (alloys, heat treatments, surface treatments, allowables), and GD&T/tolerance stack-up methodologies.
  • Analysis and Modeling: Demonstrated capability performing closed-form hand calculations and FEA analysis (linear, non-linear, buckling, modal) for high-load mechanism and structural components.
  • CAD and PLM: Extensive experience in 3D CAD modeling, mechanism layout, and drawing release (Siemens NX preferred, or equivalent like CATIA/Creo) with PLM workflows.
  • Hardware and Supplier Execution: Proven track record sourcing aerospace hardware, collaborating with specialized mechanism/actuator suppliers, and supporting physical builds and test rigs.
  • Autonomy: Demonstrated ability to self-direct, prioritize technical tasks without oversight, and deliver functional hardware under tight timelines.
  • Clearance: Secret eligible

Preferred qualifications:

  • Direct experience with UAV, autonomous aircraft, or rotorcraft landing systems and arresting gear integration.
  • Familiarity with aerospace structural, environmental, and mechanism drop-test standards (e.g., MIL-STD-810, RTCA DO-160, AS6053, MIL-A-8866/MIL-A-8867).
  • Hands-on machine shop, fabrication, or mechanical assembly experience in a prototype or rapid R&D environment.

The Opportunity:


The Pre-Production Technical Director is responsible for supporting creative and visual objectives through pipeline troubleshooting, user support, technical direction, and tool development for front-end craft groups, including Story, Edit, Art, Concept, Design, Visual Development, and Previs. As a technical expert, the Pre-Production Technical Director exhibits a deep understanding of processes, technology, and tools within these domains. They contribute technical expertise to the design and development of artist workflows and tools, ensuring that the pre-production process is efficient and integrated with the overall production pipeline. 


What You’ll Do:


Technical Responsibilities: 

  • Understand the visual requirements for productions and suggest new technologies, or design procedures, techniques, and tools to meet these requirements. 
  • Provide technical expertise and guidance for all technology within the Pre-Production department. 
  • Contribute to the direction, evolution, and maintenance of the technology within the Pre-Production Department. 
  • Design, develop, and write well-maintainable and consistently high-quality code. 
  • Track and resolve the most complex technical issues within Pre-Production in partnership with other TDs and Software Engineers. 
  • Work closely with other TDs and Software Engineers within Pre-Production to drive the technical success of key development initiatives. 
  • Ensure that technology, tools, and procedures within the Pre-Production Craft Group support the creative process. 
  • Provide solutions to visual problems through existing tools or by leading the implementation of new tools. 
  • Take responsibility for the troubleshooting and optimization of Pre-Production tools, software, and workflows. 
  • Actively drive the QA, technical testing, and validation of new technology, tool releases, or pipeline changes, ensuring artist workflow is not impacted. 
  • Understand the processes of adjoining departments and provide input where required to maximize pipeline efficiency and quality. 
  • Actively participate in brainstorming and problem-solving, contributing technical expertise and insight to create and maintain technology within the canonical production pipeline. 
  • Support the organization’s overall technical goals as required.

Bidding & Scheduling Responsibilities: 

  • Be aware of the deadlines for own development initiatives and actively engage in keeping these on track. 
  • Continuously monitor the scope of the most technically challenging development initiatives within the Pre-Production department and help to ensure scope adjustments have additional estimates, etc. 
  • Prioritize and break down technical projects into organized parts. 
  • Work with the Supervising TD to prepare estimates and pitches as required.

Talent & Performance Management Responsibilities: 

  • Work with the Supervising TD for Front-End to provide technical guidance to Pre-Production TDs with day-to-day issues and escalate through the right channels when necessary. 
  • Work with Technology Talent Management and Supervising TDs to help further develop the skills and abilities of mid-level TDs within the Front End Craft Group. 
  • Mentor mid-level TDs within the team and assist in orientation with senior new starters. 
  • Create synergies between different work groups to promote efficiency and optimization and to generate innovative ideas and approaches to how we do things.

Communication Collaboration & Relationship Development Responsibilities: 

  • Strong communication skills for technical ideas, project status, problems, requirements, rollout plans, etc. 
  • Able to communicate with Program Managers to contribute to the scheduling and planning of complex technology initiatives. 
  • Able to discuss complex issues with Senior Software Engineers, developers, and supervisors. 
  • Able to present to small teams (tool demos, Show Contract process, Support Dashboards, etc.). 
  • Good written communication skills for specs, tickets, status updates, etc.

Behaviours: 

  • Takes a collaborative approach, always working towards team goals and success.
  • Is artist-focused, passionate about improving the artist experience and workflow.
  • Acts as a proactive contributor, eager to learn and help the team succeed.
  • Stays supportive and approachable, fostering a friendly and open environment.
  • Is detail-oriented, ensuring high standards in all work.
  • Remains trustworthy and reliable in all responsibilities. 

What You’ll Need:

  • Relevant education in software engineering and/or film creation process.
  • 5+ years of proven pipeline TD experience in large-scale animated features, animated TV series, games and/or VFX feature films.
  • Proven technical achievements within feature animation or VFX.
  • An understanding of traditional techniques appropriate to the Pre-Production craft group. 
  • Comprehensive experience using and troubleshooting in relevant software such as Maya, Flix, Avid, Storyboard Pro, Premiere, Photoshop, and other related software used in the Pre-Production domain. 
  • Comprehensive understanding of technical details within the Pre-Production department. 
  • Ability to code review and troubleshoot problems as they arise. 
  • Expert knowledge in Python as well as PyQt or another GUI toolkit. 
  • Knowledge of concepts like data flow, data dependencies, metadata, publishing, and retrieval. 
  • Solid understanding of C++ is a plus. A strong understanding of USD and its general concepts. 
  • Knowledge of Flow Production Tracking (ShotGrid). 
  • Knowledge of code management software such as git and GitHub and code review processes. 
  • Knowledge of software development practices such as Agile and how to apply them in software such as Jira. 
  • Degree in Animation, Film, Computer Science, Design, Engineering, Math, or Physics, or equivalent combination of education and work experience in animation/VFX.

This role is based in Vancouver, British Columbia. Hybrid Role (Minimum requirement of 3 days a week in the office).

Job Description

The Launch Manager acts as the strategic center of every title’s journey to the members —serving as the conductor of launch excellence, a trusted expert on launch strategy, and an architect of cross-functional interactions. You own end-to-end accountability for platform launches, translating business objectives into product merchandising decisions and driving the partnerships necessary for seamless execution.


As the Launch Manager, you are the on-the-ground product expert, overseeing the lifecycle of merchandising behaviors and promotional strategy to ensure high-quality launches. You will manage the launch strategy for your local slate, serving as the connective tissue that aligns cross-functional partners, mitigates risks, and drives member value.


Across each of these dimensions, you will bring proactive judgment, clear communication of tradeoffs, and a relentless drive to surface the right solution at the right time.


In this role you will:


As the Conductor of Launch Excellence

  • Serve as the connective tissue for End-to-end title and merchandising campaign launch — proactively gathering, centralizing, and disseminating the right context to keep all cross-functional partners aligned on priorities, dependencies, and decisions
  • Own the quality and accountability for bringing all content to life on our platform. This involves positioning, presenting and packaging the intricate web of creative assets and aligning timelines across multiple cross-functional teams.
  • Be the control tower troubleshooting high-stakes bottlenecks, and identifying risk patterns across the slate — not just single titles — to surface systemic issues before they escalate.

As a Trusted Expert on Launch Strategy

  • Be the on-the-ground product and merchandising expert for Japan, translating business, consumer, and local market objectives into clear product merchandising decisions — including knowing what not to do on platform and why.
  • Partner deeply with local Content and Marketing teams to architect data-driven strategies for content discovery that is optimized for member experience
  • Evaluate novel and complex asks — weighing impact, risk, dependencies, and opportunity cost — and apply sound judgment on when to proceed, push back, or escalate.
  • Proactively surface the real issue beneath the ask — diagnosing root causes and bringing forward solutions, not just flagging problems.

As an Architect of cross-functional Interactions

  • Build strong bridges and tight partnerships with cross-functional partner teams
  • Effectively communicate context, priorities, and trade-offs to our partner teams with regards to established title merchandising levers and launch strategies
  • Support and influence new strategies and workflows to increase impact and launch excellence.
  • Encourage and model risk-taking, data-informed decision-making, and constant innovation.
  • Serve as the primary point of escalation for title-level merchandise and launch issues or failures.


 

Role Requirements:


  • Minimum 5-7 years of project management experience in a fast-paced and agile environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to translate business and consumer objectives into product strategy, with strong intuition for what 'good' looks like in a launch context.
  • Systems thinker who can identify patterns across a portfolio, evaluate tradeoffs rigorously, and communicate risks and recommendations persuasively to diverse stakeholders.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills in Japanese and English
  • Strong relationship management and expectation-setting skills.
  • Track record of modeling accountability and ability to collaborate, influence, and partner effectively with internal stakeholders.
  • An earnest and inclusive team player who will be a great steward of the Netflix culture

We hold ourselves to the highest standards in fulfilling our obligations to investment partners, host nations, and end-user customers. To support the continued success of these long-term, strategically important projects, Microsoft is seeking world-class talent to lead and strengthen subsea operations across our portfolio.

This role supports submarine cable systems that are critical to Microsoft’s cloud and AI capabilities, enabling services used by millions of consumers and businesses worldwide. We are looking for an experienced, courageous, and adaptable professional with strong hands-on experience in submarine cable route design, route engineering, and project implementation who can support, influence, and deliver network infrastructure in a fast-paced production environment. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong analytical, communication, people-management, and collaboration skills, with the ability to work across diverse teams, influence stakeholders, and deliver measurable business impact.

In alignment with Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment where all employees can contribute positively to our culture every day.



Responsibilities

The Senior Subsea Project and Operations Manager will be responsible for managing, standardizing, and driving steady-state execution across key areas of Microsoft’s subsea investment portfolio. This role carries deep responsibility for submarine cable projects and operations across multiple systems.

  • Partner with Microsoft network investment and commercial managers to bring an operator-focused perspective to submarine consortium and joint-investment engagements on a system-by-system basis.
  • Act as an active and key contributor in consortium and committee meetings, particularly CCM, IPG, MWG, and TWG, to effectively represent Microsoft’s needs and interests.

  • Plan, communicate, and execute against budgets for system upgrade plans.
  • Work closely with procurement organizations to plan annual purchase orders, execute contracts as required, and maintain a predictable business rhythm.
  • Serve as the escalation point and remediation expert for matters related to Microsoft-owned cable systems, cable landing station infrastructure, access-related works, Network Operations Centers, and data center interfaces across multiple systems.

  • Develop and maintain internal repositories to ensure secure access to information related to all aspects of Microsoft’s involvement in contracted subsea programs.
  • Represent Microsoft and/or specific systems externally with environmental groups and third-party industry committees where close cooperation is required to protect and sustain system health.

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations and Innovation (CO+I) team builds and operates Microsoft datacenters, which in turn powers Microsoft’s cloud business. The CO+I Engineering team (CO+IE) delivers services, applications, and automation supporting datacenter planning, construction, and operation. We own a large portfolio of services, including workflows that enable predicable, lowest cost datacenter construction, telemetry systems that drive high availability and optimized energy usage, and task and performance management applications that help our operation run as efficiently as possible. CO+I Engineering is a competitive advantage for Microsoft, and an important pillar in its cloud success.

The Technical Program Manager of Critical Infrastructure Delivery will deliver complex network infrastructure projects, working with multi-faceted teams (full time employees and vendor staff) and have technical depth and experience in delivering bare metal infrastructure at scale, in operational environments.  The successful candidate will be a team player, possess solid communication and collaboration skills, and have the ability to effectively manage and solve problems in alignment to standards and schedule.  The role partners closely with colleagues, engineering and other infrastructure and operational teams, along with key decision makers across geographic and organizational boundaries, while maintaining excellence in installation of network infrastructure for high security networks in datacenters and other spaces.

  • You will partner with hardware Engineering to design technical solutions deployable in the field. You’ll also  identify risks and propose data-driven mitigations.

  • You will deliver on roadmaps for multiple bare metal field delivery pillars, track project schedules, develop staging and implementation plans, and ensure reporting data is in place to support governance programs.
  • You’ll lead teams to partner with other departments to collect performance metrics, drive customer support, and lead direct field engagements.
  • Manage relationships and expectations with various business stakeholders across CO+I.
  • Create and contribute to processes, procedures, and tools to drive continuous improvements in execution.
  • Participate in regular and annual planning strategies, including budget, contract execution that encompasses current and future scope commitments.

Site Reliability engineering manager owns >99% compute uptime outcome, drives unplanned facilities compute losses to 0, ensures efficient allocation of > 3GW site power, upgrade robust fault-free megapack failover systems capable of supporting all halls for >4 hours (160 MWhr per hall), drives robust hardware inventory systems and repair velocity to eliminate hardware chokepoints.

    • Lead robustification of documentation workflow

We are looking for a Mechanical Engineer to aid the technical development of a holistic support system for service, maintenance, deployment, launch, and recovery of the Copperhead family of vehicles. ABOUT THE TEAM
Our Warfighter Systems division is pioneering a future where mixed reality (MR), creates immersive, intuitive, and life-saving technologies. By seamlessly integrating real-time data with cutting-edge visualization tools, we are empowering warfighters with unparalleled situational awareness, enhanced training experiences, and operational superiority. This team is consistently pushing the boundaries of what's possible, and shaping a future where technology and defense unite to protect our nation.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:
As a Staff Electrical Engineer, you will be part of an exclusive CEO-priority program to deliver a soldier-portable, auto-aiming counter-UAS system (actuator-driven steerable platform, CV models, LIDAR ballistic calculator, onboard power/compute). Your mission is simple and urgent: ensure U.S. warfighters don't get attacked by drones. You will take an existing prototype and drive it through ruggedization and into a Weapon Systems production-ready design with components and processes that can be manufactured at scale.


YOU WILL:

  • Own the electrical architecture end-to-end, assessing the existing prototype, documenting tribal knowledge, and identifying EE-specific gaps across power, sensing, compute, and actuator drive subsystems.

  • Demonstrated experience taking hardware from bench prototype through ruggedization to early manufacturing (prototype-to-production).
  • Familiarity with actuator dynamics — bandwidth, force, and speed trade-offs — and the associated drive electronics and control systems.
  • Breadth across EE subsystems, including electro-optical/IR sensors, power and compute board design, and closed-loop control systems.
  • Ability to author and execute pragmatic test plans, interpret results, and change course when required to deliver a working product on an aggressive timeline.
  • A self-starter mentality, capable of identifying problems, proposing innovative solutions, and executing with minimal oversight.
  • U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export-controlled data.

  • Experience designing for soldier-portable platforms with an instinct for practical SWaP and ergonomic constraints.

The B2B Content team helps business audiences understand what AI makes possible and how to put it to work. We develop narrative, editorial, demo, and adoption programs that connect OpenAI’s products to concrete business value.

We partner closely with Product Marketing, Demand Generation, Customer Education, Sales, and other teams to create content that is useful on its own and supports the broader customer journey.

We value people who are eager to learn, have a bias for action, and look beyond the immediate deliverable. We build the tools, systems, and shared practices that help the whole team produce better work over time.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Content Marketing Manager, Demand Generation to turn foundational B2B messaging, flagship narratives, research, launches, events, and product workflows into the right content for different industries, lines of business, audiences, and stages of the customer journey.

You’ll create content across webinars, guides, ebooks, blogs, customer proof, and decision-enablement materials. You’ll also build the modular frameworks that allow strong source material to be adapted and reused without recreating the work from scratch.

You’ll work closely with Product Marketing, which owns product positioning and messaging, and Demand Generation, which owns audience and channel strategy. You’ll bring strong content judgment to that partnership: helping determine what should be created, how it should be structured, and how it can work across different contexts while preserving a coherent central narrative.

This is a senior individual-contributor role for a hands-on marketer, writer, and editor. It does not include people management or ownership of the broader content portfolio.

This is a hybrid role and will be based in San Francisco, Monday through Wednesday. Thursday and Friday are work-from-home days, with occasional in-office attendance as needed for live webinars.

In this role, you will

  • Partner with Product Marketing, Demand Generation, the Senior Narrative Writer, the Adoption Content Marketer, and Demo Studio to identify strong source material and define the content plan for priority programs.

  • Create and adapt content across webinars, flagship guides and ebooks, thought-leadership blogs, solution and buyer guides, customer proof, and decision-enablement materials.

  • Turn core assets into reusable modules for specific industries, lines of business, use cases, and executive, practitioner, and technical audiences.

  • Develop awareness-, consideration-, and decision-stage versions of priority content while preserving the central narrative.

  • Find the strongest narrative, proof point, or value proposition within complex source material and translate it into clear, useful content.

  • Collaborate with Demand Generation and channel partners to ensure content is designed for real audience and distribution needs.

  • Use audience and performance signals to improve how future content is structured, packaged, and reused.

  • Establish repeatable frameworks, templates, and practices that increase the return on major content investments.

  • Maintain strong editorial quality across a high volume of interconnected assets.

You might thrive in this role if you

  • Have 7+ years of experience in B2B content marketing, editorial, integrated campaigns, or a related discipline.

  • Are an exceptional writer and editor with a portfolio showing how you adapted substantive source material for different B2B audiences and contexts.

  • Can translate complex B2B product and business subject matter into content that is clear without becoming simplistic.

  • Know how to identify the strongest B2B narrative, proof point, or value proposition within a larger body of material.

  • Have experience creating B2B content across industries, business functions, buyer groups, or stages of the customer journey.

  • Understand B2B audience and channel needs and can collaborate closely with Demand Generation without losing the integrity of the central narrative.

  • Can create both high-quality individual assets and the systems that make future work faster and more consistent.

  • Combine strong editorial judgment with speed, precision, and comfort working across a high volume of interconnected work.

About Scale

Scale builds AI systems for decisions that matter. We started out providing the data and evaluation behind many of the world's leading models, and we still work with the major frontier labs on research and post-training. Today we also build full applications: we take an organisation's own data and expertise, forward deploy alongside their teams, and build the systems they come to rely on, powered by the Scale GenAI Platform.

The Role

Defence is under pressure to adopt AI at pace. The 2025 Strategic Defence Review and the Defence AI Strategy push for AI to move from experiment to operational capability, Defence Digital and UK Strategic Command are driving digital and data programmes across the department, and the enabling organisations are being asked to field reliable systems, not pilots. Scale wants to play a foundational role in building the dependable AI applications that shift depends on.

We're looking for someone to lead that work across UK defence and the national security community. You'd own our commercial relationships across the Ministry of Defence and its enabling organisations - Defence Digital, UK Strategic Command, DE&S, and Dstl - and the broader defence and security customer base.

This is a critical role reporting directly to the new Public Sector leader. You'd carry a number, win deals yourself, and build a small team behind you as the work grows. It suits someone who has sold into defence before and knows how it actually makes decisions, not just how the org charts look.

What you'll do

  • Own our commercial plan and pipeline for UK defence and security
  • Find, shape, and close deals yourself, from the first conversation through to contract and into delivery
  • Use the relationships you already have across the MOD, Defence Digital, UK Strategic Command, DE&S, Dstl, and the security and intelligence community
  • Work the defence routes to market, and know which are worth the effort and which aren't (the Defence Sourcing Portal, DASA, JOSCAR registration, single-source arrangements, and the main CCS frameworks)
  • Be a credible counterpart to senior military and civil service leaders, and turn what they need into work we can actually deliver
  • Navigate the security clearance, accreditation, and information-handling requirements that come with defence work
  • Stay close to our product and delivery teams so what we sell is what we build
  • Hire and lead a small team over time, and help shape the wider UK public sector plan as a team with the Central Government Lead and Public Sector leader.

What we're looking for

  • You've sold and delivered AI technology or transformation work into UK defence or national security, either from a vendor or SI or from inside the MOD or the Armed Forces
  • You know at least one part of defence well (MOD, UK Strategic Command, DE&S, Dstl, or a single Service) and how it buys
  • You’ve rolled up your sleeves and built something from scratch, whether that’s a new vertical, territory or product launch
  • You understand defence and public sector procurement: frameworks, tenders, single-source rules, and buying that runs through a lot of stakeholders
  • You've opened doors, run complex pursuits, and owned the result
  • You have relationships with senior people in defence
  • You hold, or are eligible to obtain, UK security clearance (SC as a minimum; DV desirable)
  • You do your best work when things are ambiguous and moving quickly

People who tend to fit this have spent years leading UK defence work at companies like Palantir, Anduril, BAE Systems, QinetiQ, Leidos or Babcock, at consultancies and systems integrators like Accenture, Deloitte, EY or PA Consulting, or in senior commercial or programme roles inside the MOD, DE&S, or the Armed Forces.

Nice to have

  • Experience with AI or data-heavy platforms
  • Regulated, mission-critical, or classified government programmes
  • You've built or run a small commercial team before

Why join

You'd be building this market, not maintaining it. There's no playbook to inherit, which is rather the point. The deals you win, and the way you win them, will shape how Scale works with UK defence for years.

You'd own our commercial relationships across civilian departments, starting where the near-term pipeline is strongest: HMRC, DWP, and NHS.

You'd be building this market, not maintaining it. There's no playbook to inherit, which is rather the point. The deals you win, and the way you win them, will shape how Scale works with UK government for years.

About the role

Anthropic’s Applied AI team helps the world’s largest organizations put Claude to work. As a Cybersecurity Specialist on Applied AI, you’ll be part of an overlay team of domain experts who sit alongside our enterprise account teams and bring deep security expertise to the accounts where it matters most.

You won’t own an account. You’ll be the security expert the account team pulls in to win and grow the most important security conversations: helping CISOs and security leaders see where Claude can take on real security work, then guiding them from early pilots to durable, production workloads. You’ll cover a portfolio of enterprise accounts across regulated industries like financial services, insurance, and healthcare, strategic accounts like semiconductors (IP protection, industrial control systems, export controls), and digital natives and public sector agencies, each with its own threat model.

How this team works

  • You partner with account executives, account architects, and generalist Applied AI engineers, who own the customer relationship and the broader technical engagement. You bring the security depth they don’t have time to build.
  • You work across many accounts at once, so the playbooks, reference implementations, and evaluation approaches you build are reused across the field, not just for one customer.
  • You are the connection point between the field and Anthropic’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams, turning what you see in customer security programs into product feedback.
  • You work alongside ISVs, systems integrators, and managed security providers who already serve these customers, enabling them where they own the engagement rather than competing with them.

Responsibilities

  • Join account teams to understand a customer’s security program, identify where Claude can do meaningful security work, and turn that into a technical plan and business case
  • Serve as the security-domain technical advisor on strategic enterprise accounts, from discovery through deployment
  • Move customers from one-time code scanning to sustained security workloads: application security in the SDLC, continuous automated penetration testing, alert triage and investigation, and threat intelligence that answers “does this new vulnerability affect us, and where”
  • Build and maintain reference implementations, harnesses, and evaluation approaches, and help customers adapt them to their own environments and controls
  • Run workshops and hands-on sessions where customer security teams use Claude on their own code and workflows
  • Equip partners to deliver Claude-powered security outcomes, with a clear line between what Anthropic delivers and what partners deliver
  • Speak credibly to every audience, from appsec engineers to CISOs and executives, including how to explain the value and risk of security work in business terms
  • Define and track adoption depth for each security workload across your accounts, and work with Product and Engineering on the telemetry to measure it
  • Write the playbooks and best practices the rest of the field can reuse, including how Claude complements the security tooling customers already own
  • Develop reference customers who can speak to the value they’re realizing
  • Stay current on frontier LLM capabilities and the new classes of vulnerabilities and attacks they surface
  • Travel occasionally to customer sites for workshops and technical deep dives

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Maritime Digital Production (MDP) is the software and digital systems function within Anduril's Heavy Metal division. We build the software-defined shipyard. That means the full technology stack running Anduril's shipbuilding factories: the data infrastructure that makes every machine and sensor visible in real time, ArsenalOS (our manufacturing execution system that workers and planners use every shift), the scheduling engine that replans production in minutes instead of days, and the AI systems that eliminate manual toil from both the shop floor and business operations.

This work is anchored by Arsenal-2, our software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base. ArsenalOS is the digital backbone of that yard. It connects fabrication and outfitting to material movement and inspection. Planners get one real-time view of production. We aren't waiting for the yard to open. Development is already underway here in Orange County, California. The team is proving out the manufacturing methods and digital workflows that will scale across the shipyard network.

MDP operates at the boundary between Operational Technology and Information Technology. Our systems live where factory-floor machines, edge compute, and OT networks meet enterprise platforms and cloud infrastructure. We incubate solutions close to the production line, validate them with real operators building real hardware, harden them for reliability and security, and then scale them across multiple sites. The environment is fast, physical, and consequential. When our systems go down, production stops. The output of our work is not a dashboard: it is a ship.

This is not a support function. It is a strategic investment by Anduril in the premise that digitizing the manufacturing lifecycle end-to-end, from engineering definition through scheduling through execution through field feedback, is how Heavy Metal will out-build, out-adapt, and out-scale the traditional defense industrial base. MDP is scaling from a founding team to 70+ engineers across multiple U.S. sites. You will be joining early, working on hard problems with real operational stakes, and shaping how manufacturing software is built at Anduril from the ground up.

ABOUT THE JOB

MDP is building the manufacturing digital thread that connects engineering release to the machines and inspection systems on the factory floor. You'll own the Development and integration integration layer between Teamcenter and Anduril's ArsenalOS platform so CAM programs, CAI/CMM programs, tools and fixtures, and inspection results move automatically instead of by hand.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Build and own the integrations that carry CAM and CAI data out of Teamcenter and onto the shop floor, including NX CAM outputs, DNC dispatch to machine controls and the return path for as-run data.
  • Develop custom Teamcenter extensions using ITK and SOA, along with BMIDE data model changes and Active Workspace interfaces, to support manufacturing workflows that off-the-shelf configuration can't reach.
  • Close the inspection loop by integrating CAI and metrology systems so measured results land back in the digital thread as structured data rather than static reports.
  • Make EBOM to MBOM propagation and model-based definition data flow automatically into downstream manufacturing and quality systems.
  • Unblock partner teams across scheduling, applied AI and manufacturing systems by exposing manufacturing data through APIs they can build on.
  • Partner with manufacturing engineers and factory operators to understand production workflows and translate them into software requirements.
  • Write production-quality code with comprehensive tests, participating in code review and architectural discussions.
  • Deploy and operate your systems in factory environments, including edge compute clusters and OT networks.
  • Leverage AI tooling (coding assistants, automation) in your development workflow and contribute to team engineering practices.
  • Join an on-call rotation supporting production factory systems.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of experience in a software engineering role building production systems, ideally in a fast-paced environment.
  • Deep expertise in Teamcenter development: 5+ years hands-on with ITK and SOA customization in C++ and Java, BMIDE data modeling and Active Workspace.
  • Demonstrated experience building custom Teamcenter handlers, services and integrations, not only configuring workflows and templates.
  • Working knowledge of manufacturing data domains, including CAM, CAI, CMM, and NC programming outputs, machine dispatch, metrology and inspection data, and the relationship between EBOM and MBOM.
  • Experience authoring and developing NX Open programs to automate NX/Design Center workflows.
  • Strong technical fluency in modern software architectures, APIs, distributed systems, CI/CD, and cloud or edge infrastructure.
  • Experience building systems that must operate reliably under real-world operational constraints (high availability, low latency, or constrained environments).
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to collaborate across engineering, manufacturing, and operations teams.
  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related technical field, or equivalent practical
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in manufacturing, industrial, or OT-adjacent domains (MES, SCADA, PLC integration, factory automation, IoT).
  • Hands-on experience with CAM and CAI toolchains such as NX CAM, Vericut and PolyWorks, and with industrial data protocols such as MTConnect and OPC-UA.
  • Familiarity with model-based definition standards including STEP AP242, ASME Y14.41 and CAD PMI, and with QIF for inspection data exchange.
  • Familiarity with frontier AI tooling, AI coding assistants, and AI-enabled software development workflows.
  • Experience in hyper-growth startup-like environments, with demonstrated success balancing speed, ambiguity, and long-term system health.
  • Familiarity with enterprise systems such as ERP, MES, WMS, or manufacturing planning systems.
  • Experience in manufacturing industries with hands-on exposure to assembly lines or production environments.

The Maneuver Dominance team is building Thunder - an autonomous attack rotorcraft built to fight alongside crewed combat aviation to deliver overwhelming mass effects deep beyond the front lines.
