The Senior Finance Manager owns Defect Cost Controllership across NA, the single source of truth for $3+B in direct defect costs spanning Damages, Concessions, and unsellable inventory. The function provides Operations and Finance leaders with the cost attribution and P&L mapping required to set reduction targets, assess workstream performance, and commit to operating plans. The complexity is threefold: (1) scope spans the full defect cost chain from site-level operational defects through Liquidations account treatment across cost types with no pre-existing standardized financial framework; (2) the function must maintain 100% NA site coverage across a continuously expanding network without gaps in controllership or reporting continuity; and (3) defect cost sits at the intersection of Operations, Accounting, and E2E Supply Chain, requiring this role to ensure financial data is simultaneously actionable for operations leadership, audit-ready for finance, and consistent enough to anchor the kingpin commitments that flow into quarterly and annual operating plans.

This role owns Inventory Quality Finance with controllership accountability across warehouse damages, inventory adjustments, removals and returns, and SOX compliance for global inventory. The function governs approximately $3-4B in inventory adjustments annually, a cost base where accounting treatment gaps carry direct SOX exposure. The role governs inventory controllership at three distinct levels simultaneously: reserve calculation methodology (replacing intuition-based approaches with data-driven models), Inventory Roll-Forward account ownership (serving as the primary coordination point with Accounting), and SOX controllership framework design for global inventory.

Overview

Conversational commerce introduces challenges that differ from traditional web shopping. Preferences emerge through dialogue, expectations for accuracy and trust are high, and systems must reason over context and frequently changing commerce data.

Microsoft Copilot is building shopping experiences that are conversational, proactive, and trustworthy. As a Senior Applied Science Lead, you will be hands on and lead the development of machine learning and generative AI systems that power product discovery, ranking, personalization, and reasoning across Copilot, Bing and Edge Shopping surfaces. This role sits at the intersection of applied machine learning, generative AI, and product experience, with clear ownership of core shopping intelligence used directly in user-facing experiences.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities
  • Design, build, and productionize machine learning models for product discovery, ranking, recommendation, and personalization using large-scale commerce and behavioral data.
  • Develop LLM-based systems for conversational shopping, including prompt design, retrieval-augmented generation, tool orchestration, and grounding against structured commerce data.
  • Address quality and trust challenges such as hallucination risk, stale data, and recommendation reliability.
  • Define evaluation frameworks and experimentation strategies for conversational and proactive shopping scenarios, including offline metrics and online experiments.
  • Partner closely with product, engineering, and design teams to translate models into low-latency, reliable Copilot experiences.
  • Provide technical leadership for applied science within Copilot Shopping through design reviews, mentoring, and setting quality standards.
  • Contribute to model governance and Responsible AI practices to ensure trustworthy and compliant systems.

We build the platform that decides how AI traffic flows across Microsoft's global infrastructure, so services like Azure OpenAI and Microsoft Copilot stay fast and reliable. You'll join a supportive, connected team that keeps these experiences fair and dependable for every customer while making the most of every GPU we run.
 
As a Senior Software Engineer, AI Infrastructure on our team, you'll design, build, and run services that route and prioritize AI requests and match them to available computing capacity. You'll own the design of key parts of our platform, work with partner teams to bring new AI models and capabilities to customers, and help keep our services healthy in production. This opportunity will allow you to deepen your knowledge of distributed systems at global scale, learn how the world's leading AI models are served, and grow as a technical leader and mentor on your team.
 
Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.


Responsibilities
  • Design - Own the design of key parts of our platform for routing AI traffic and managing computing capacity. Write design proposals, compare options, and make sure designs meet goals for speed, reliability, scale, and cost.
  • Coding - Write clear, secure, well-tested code and set a good example for the team. Give thoughtful, timely code reviews that help others grow.
  • Implement - Break work into clear, dependable milestones with program managers. Use feature flags and gradual rollouts to test changes safely, measure their impact, and roll back quickly when needed.
  • Reliability and Supportability - Take part in the on-call rotation as a designated responsible individual (DRI). Add monitoring and dashboards, improve troubleshooting guides, and help reduce how often incidents happen.
  • Understand User Requirements - Work with product managers and partner teams to understand what customers need and turn those needs into clear technical requirements.
  • Engineering Excellence - Build security, privacy, and compliance into every stage of your work, from design to deployment. Automate testing and releases, and share what you learn with the team.
  • AI-Native Development - Use artificial intelligence (AI) tools across the software development lifecycle (SDLC), from writing code and tests to investigating live issues. Take responsibility for AI-generated work and help teammates do the same.
  • Embody our Culture and Values 

 



Qualifications

Required Qualifications: 

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 4+ years technical engineering experience building distributed systems with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C#, Java, or Go
    • OR equivalent experience. 
Other Requirements
  • Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
    • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud Background Check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter. 
Preferred Qualifications
  • Master's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 6+ years technical engineering experience building distributed systems with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C#, Java, or Go
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field
      • AND 8+ years technical engineering experience building distributed systems with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C#, Java, or Go
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 3+ years of experience running distributed services on public cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS), or Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
  • 2+ years of experience with systems that route or schedule traffic, or that allocate computing resources.
  • Experience with Python, Docker, and Kubernetes.
  • Experience with AI or machine learning (ML) infrastructure, such as serving models in production or managing GPU fleets.
  • Experience delivering projects with partner teams, from design through launch and operation.
  • Experience being on call for highly available services and improving monitoring to reduce incidents.

Overview
Moving data reliably at cloud scale is one of the hardest problems in the industry, and it is the foundation every analytics and AI scenario depends on. On the Fabric Data Factory team, you will build and own the Data Factory workload within Microsoft Fabric, the unified analytics platform. You will work on pipelines, dataflows, and related tooling that help customers move, transform, and orchestrate large volumes of data across diverse sources and destinations. Your work will sit at the intersection of distributed systems, big data engineering, and cloud-native development, where you will take on challenges in throughput, fault tolerance, scalability, and cost efficiency. 
 
We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer for our Fabric Data Factory team where you will participate  across the full engineering lifecycle, from authoring experiences and runtime execution through monitoring, diagnostics, and live-site reliability. You will partner with teams across Fabric, Azure Data Factory, and Power Query to deliver enterprise-grade solutions for workloads ranging from simple data copy tasks to multi-stage ETL pipelines. This opportunity will allow you to deepen your expertise in distributed systems at cloud scale, broaden your technical influence across partner engineering teams, and grow your impact on a platform used by enterprise customers worldwide.
At Microsoft, our mission to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more guides how we partner with customers to deliver trusted, impactful solutions. With a growth mindset culture, we innovate responsibly and measure success by shared progress, people, teams, and customers. Join us to do meaningful work that changes the world and helps shape what's next for everyone.


Responsibilities
  • Designs and owns core Data Factory artifacts, including pipelines and dataflows, that support enterprise-scale data integration workloads with high throughput, fault tolerance, and performance.
  • Understands customer and user requirements for a project or sub-section of a product and translates them into technical designs.
  • Applies artificial intelligence (AI) tools responsibly across the full software development lifecycle, takes ownership of AI-generated assets, and experiments to improve capabilities.
  • Leads by example in code quality by conducting timely, insightful code reviews, upholding standards, security, and compliance, and coaching engineers using automated analysis tools integrated into the build process.
  • Designs and owns test strategies that prevent regression, incorporate security testing, and cover edge and negative cases. Builds testable code from the start and identifies hard-to-test areas for future rearchitecture.
  • Leads architecture discussions for complex features by creating and iterating on design documents, evaluating trade-offs, and ensuring performance, scalability, and resiliency requirements are met.
  • Collaborates with teams across Fabric and Azure to resolve dependency and ownership conflicts.
  • Plans and delivers features with full lifecycle ownership by breaking work into tracked tasks, managing feature flighting and rollback plans, and automating deployments following safe-change practices.
  • Owns live-site reliability as a Designated Responsible Individual (DRI) by integrating telemetry and observability, responding to incidents within service-level agreements, driving postmortems and root-cause fixes, and improving troubleshooting guides and on-call practices.

NVIDIA is hiring a Principal Engineer to lead three interconnected and strategic platform charters at the intersection of information security, enterprise collaboration, and AI — forming the backbone of how NVIDIA protects sensitive content, governs enterprise data access, and powers the next generation of AI agents at scale. These platforms span sensitive-information protection and DLP, a central data governance layer that controls access to enterprise content across email, messaging, document stores, and search, and an enterprise AI knowledge platform that ingests and validates content for reliable consumption by AI agents — with a consistent focus on access control fidelity, export-control enforcement, and production readiness. This is a high-impact individual contributor role with a clear path into engineering leadership and management. We are looking for a technically strong engineer who is eager to grow beyond IC execution — someone who can own platform strategy, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and eventually step into leading and growing a team. Strong cross-functional partnership across Security, Legal, Finance, and AI platform teams is essential from day one.


What You Will Be Doing:

Sensitive Information Protection & Remediation

  • Own the roadmap for sensitive-information detection and remediation — partnering with Finance, Legal, and Security to define classification models, remediation workflows, and reporting that leadership can trust.
  • Lead build-vs-buy decisions and vendor evaluations to determine what to invest in internally versus augment with third-party DLP or search tools.

Enterprise Data Access & Governance

  • Drive production rollout and self-service onboarding for the enterprise data access platform, spanning connectors across email, messaging, document stores, and search (Outlook, Teams, Slack, Confluence, OneDrive, SharePoint, Google Drive, Glean).
  • Design and implement export-control enforcement and long-term audit logging — including authorization checks, schema design, data masking, retention, and RBAC controls. Evaluate third-party partners that could extend the platform for NVIDIA's customer-facing go-to-market motions.

Enterprise AI Knowledge Platform

  • Drive integration of enterprise content sources — document stores, wikis, and cloud drives — into the AI knowledge platform, ensuring content is accurate, fresh, and access-controlled for agent consumption.
  • Define production readiness gates and maintain a clear ownership boundary: this team owns integration correctness and quality, not full platform operations.

Leadership & Cross-functional Coordination

  • Serve as the technical lead across all three workstreams, aligning stakeholders in Security, Finance, Legal, and AI platform teams and driving clarity on ownership and priorities.
  • Mentor engineers and foster a culture of documentation, runbooks, and operational rigor; demonstrate readiness to grow into an engineering management role.

What We Need To See:

  • Bachelor's or Master's Degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, or a related field (or equivalent experience).
  • 15+ years of experience building and operating large-scale enterprise platforms, with a track record of growing technical scope and influence beyond individual execution.
  • Strong foundation in backend systems, distributed systems, and high-performance computing — experience with large-scale data processing, indexing pipelines, and systems designed for reliability and scale.
  • Background in enterprise security, data governance, or compliance platforms — familiarity with classification, remediation workflows, access control models, and audit requirements is a plus.
  • Experience building or integrating secure API platforms, data connectors, or enterprise SaaS integrations at scale (e.g., Confluence, SharePoint, Google Drive, Slack, Teams, or similar).
  • Proven ability to drive cross-functional alignment across Security, Legal, Finance, and platform engineering teams.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills; ability to translate complex technical tradeoffs into executive-level clarity.
  • Demonstrated interest in growing into engineering leadership — experience mentoring peers, leading projects, or taking on informal leadership responsibilities is a strong signal.
  • Comfortable holding ambiguity and driving decisions in a fast-paced, high-stakes environment.

Ways to Stand Out From The Crowd:

  • Experience with AI/LLM data pipelines, vector stores, or RAG architectures — particularly in connecting enterprise content sources to AI platforms with strict access controls.
  • Hands-on experience with Databricks or similar platforms for audit logging, data governance, and RBAC. Familiarity with Glean or similar enterprise search/DLP products and their integration patterns.
  • Experience with vendor evaluation and build-vs-buy decisions for enterprise security or content platforms.
  • Ability to leverage AI and agentic automation to drive operational efficiency and reduce engineering toil.
  • Track record of leading platform migrations, tenant consolidations, or governance modernization efforts.

We’re looking for a Senior Power Architecture & Optimization Engineer to push the limits of energy efficiency using advanced analytics and AI, including LLMs trained specifically for power analysis.

NVIDIA’s leadership in accelerated computing depends on building the most energy‑efficient GPUs and SoCs in the industry. As AI and graphics workloads scale explosively, we believe that Power Analysis and Optimization driven by AI and LLMs is the future—and a key differentiator for our next generations of GPUs and Tegra SoCs. In this role, you’ll be at the center of that effort—combining power architecture expertise with machine learning, reinforcement learning, data analytics, and large language models (LLMs) to invent new ways to model, analyze, and optimize energy consumption across full‑chip and unit‑level designs.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Analyze full‑chip and unit‑level power using internal and industry‑standard RTL and gate‑level power tools, and translate data into concrete design and architectural improvements.

  • Develop and productionize power‑aware models and flows, including ML/RL‑based techniques for anomaly detection, dynamic power management, and design‑space exploration.

  • Design and train new LLMs that “learn the art” of power analysis from design data, power reports, bug histories, and best practices—so they can:

    • Assist engineers in interpreting complex power data

    • Propose likely root causes and candidate fixes

    • Recommend architectural and micro‑architectural optimizations for power

  • Perform comparative power analysis across workloads, products, and design options to identify trends, anomalies, and optimization opportunities that aren’t obvious from first principles alone.

  • Partner closely with Architects, Performance, Software, ASIC Design, and Physical Design teams to interpret power data, root‑cause power bugs, and drive fixes and design changes.

  • Prototype and evaluate new architectural features in Verilog, with a strong focus on their power and energy implications.

  • Automate and scale flows (Python/Perl/C++), and define new pipelines that fast‑track power anomaly detection and close the loop between power data, AI models, and design decisions.

  • Apply AI to power optimization: build and deploy data‑driven models—using machine learning, reinforcement learning, data analytics, and custom LLMs—to recommend or automatically tune power‑efficient configurations and policies.

What We Need To See:

The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research Audio team works on technologies that help people hear and communicate better in everyday life, from spatial audio to hearing assistance on AI glasses. Recent work includes Conversation Focus, which helps people hear the person they're talking to in noisy environments. As wearable devices become part of daily life, understanding how people actually listen, attend, and communicate in real-world settings is central to building audio experiences that adapt to each person. We are looking for interns who want to model how people listen and communicate in the real world. Using multimodal, egocentric data from wearable devices (eye and head movement, speech and vocal behavior, gesture, and the acoustic scene), the intern will build models that infer listening and communication states such as auditory attention, listening effort, and conversational engagement. Ground truth for these states is often sparse or ambiguous. The goal is to inform hearing assistance and audio technologies that adapt to the listener. The role suits candidates with a background in machine learning, computer science, hearing science, or auditory or cognitive neuroscience, who want to work at the intersection of those fields. Successful candidates will combine strong quantitative and machine learning skills with an understanding of human hearing and communication. Specific projects will be designed with successful applicants to match their skills and experience to current research needs. Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

Responsibilities

  • Develop novel machine learning and statistical models that infer listening and communication behavior from multimodal wearable data (for example gaze, head movement, vocal cues, and turn-taking dynamics), with applications to hearing assistance.
  • Relate model outputs to established hearing science measures, such as speech intelligibility, listening effort, and self-reported communication difficulty, to validate what the models capture.
  • Design data collection strategies, benchmarks, and metrics for models trained on limited or ambiguous ground truth, including data from listeners with and without hearing loss.
  • Design, run, and analyze human subjects experiments in laboratory and naturalistic listening environments.
  • Collaborate with researchers and engineers across hearing science, audio signal processing, machine learning, and perception science.
  • Communicate the research agenda, progress, and full analyses of results.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining, a PhD in machine learning, computer science, hearing science, or auditory or cognitive neuroscience, or a related field
  • 2+ years of experience with Python or a similar language for data analysis and modeling
  • 2+ years of experience in statistical modeling and/or machine learning at the doctoral level, including time-series or sequential data
  • Research experience with one or more of the following: multimodal behavioral data (e.g., eye tracking, motion, physiological, or speech signals), speech perception, auditory attention, or conversational communication
  • Must obtain work authorization in the country of employment at the time of hire, and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Proven track record of results as demonstrated by grants, fellowships, patents, or first-authored publications at venues such as ARO, ASA/JASA, Ear and Hearing, Trends in Hearing, JSLHR, ICASSP, Interspeech, ICMI, ETRA, CHI, NeurIPS, or similar
  • Experience with deep learning frameworks such as PyTorch, including multimodal or sequence models
  • Experience with data from wearable or egocentric sensors (e.g., eye tracking, IMU, head-worn microphones), especially in naturalistic or conversational settings
  • Experience with hearing-impaired populations, hearing aids, or cochlear implants
  • Experience modeling under limited data, weak labels, or ambiguous ground truth
  • Experience working with large, high-dimensional datasets from multiple sources
  • Experience working and communicating cross-functionally in a team environment
  • Intent to return to a degree program after the completion of the internship/co-op

Reality Labs (RL) at Meta develops and builds cutting-edge Virtual and Augmented Reality products and related Accessories. The role of a Supply Planner is high-impact and complex. The Supply Planner is responsible for end-to-end supply chain planning and will act as the single point of contact for global supply availability for the products in their portfolio. This spans capacity and factory scheduling, leading the supply input into the weekly (tactical) and monthly (strategic) Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) processes, managing ex-factory and supply commit processes at contract manufacturing sites, and steering all stages of inventory planning from New Product Introduction (NPI) to End of Life (EOL) for hero products and accessories. The role requires the ability to formulate and solve constrained optimization problems across multi-tier supply networks, model yield dynamics for technically complex modules, incorporate component-level technical specifications — such as battery degradation behavior, etc. — that impact build feasibility and product longevity across the program lifecycle, and develop a deep understanding of NPI ramp plans to align production ramp-up schedules with yield, capacity readiness, and launch timelines.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the single point of contact for global supply planning and product availability for the products in their portfolio
  • Engage in the monthly S&OP activities for assigned products, providing recommendations for finished goods, materials, and capacity plans informed by yield-adjusted output models and constraint analysis
  • Engage in the weekly S&OE process for assigned products, providing information to cross-functional teams to support supply and demand planning objectives
  • Develop weekly capacity/material constrained production plans (Build Plan/Master Production Schedule) to fulfill the requirements created in the Demand Plan. Formulate these as constrained optimization problems — defining objective functions (e.g., maximize fill rate, minimize total landed cost), decision variables (allocation quantities, line assignments, build sequences), and constraints (capacity limits, component lead times, MOQs, contractual commitments) — and leverage internal planning tools and solvers to arrive at optimized solutions
  • Accountable for creating, communicating, and monitoring detailed requested ship plans at the contract manufacturing sites (forecast, commitments, build plans, PO creation)
  • Understand multi-channel demand signals for the products in the assigned portfolios and provide actionable recommendations to respond to and adjust trends (e-commerce, retail, enterprise, non-revenue)
  • Accountable for the identification and resolution of supply issues, including assisting in sourcing materials, communication, escalation, and coordination of resolution
  • Develop and manage inbound priorities using constraint-based allocation logic to ensure critical path materials are sequenced for maximum production efficiency
  • Incorporate component-level technical specifications — such as battery cycle life, degradation curves, and state-of-charge thresholds — into planning models to ensure finished goods inventory is built and sustained across the entire program lifetime while maintaining desired charging levels for a high-quality customer experience (CX)
  • Assess and model yield rates for technically complex modules (e.g., optical waveguides, display stacks, battery cells) to derive accurate production output forecasts
  • Account for yield ramp curves during NPI, steady-state yield variability in mass production, and fallout rates at key process steps to ensure build plans reflect achievable output rather than theoretical capacity
  • Partner with NPI Operations and factory teams to develop optimized capacity plans that balance production throughput requirements against overall CapEx investment, ensuring capital-efficient line configurations and equipment utilization across the manufacturing network
  • Partner with Channel Operations, NPI Operations, Sales, and other cross-functional teams to plan and execute successful product launches — aligning supply readiness, channel fill requirements, regional allocation strategies, and go-to-market timelines
  • Create and maintain inventory plans for finished goods across regional DCs considering operational and fulfillment service policies, financial targets, and cost-effective transportation considerations
  • Partner with Contract Manufacturing Operations to ensure that site capacities are properly modeled and optimized across the network in meeting customer demand, incorporating line-level throughput constraints and changeover times into planning models
  • Partner with Sourcing teams to develop sourcing strategies for technically complex modules — providing demand signals, and supply risk inputs that inform supplier qualification, dual-source decisions, and capacity reservation strategies
  • Accountable for supply chain key performance indicators (KPIs) associated with the assigned product portfolio — including plan adherence, inventory turns, and fill rate
  • Lead automation and development initiatives related to planning systems and tools — including solver integration, optimization model development, scenario simulation engines, and data pipeline enhancements that improve planning accuracy and decision speed

  • 4+ years of experience in Supply Planning roles, preferably in Consumer Electronics, with a thorough understanding of key modules and components (e.g., battery systems, optical assemblies, display stacks) and their impact on planning strategies across the product lifecycle
  • Experience leading or participating in S&OP and S&OE processes, including providing supply plan recommendations and constraint-based capacity inputs
  • Prior experience in scenario modeling and constrained optimization — ability to build models with large data sets, define objective functions and constraints, and leverage optimization solvers to drive supply chain decisions
  • Experience in NPI launch planning, including cross-functional coordination with Operations, Channel, and Sales teams to align supply readiness, channel fill strategies, and go-to-market timelines for successful product launches

  • Experience driving decision-making through fact-based analysis and rationale

  • Experience with global manufacturing operations and contract manufacturer (CM) management, including capacity modeling, NPI ramp planning, and CapEx optimization across multi-site networks

  • You are the connection point between the field and Anthropic’s Product, Research, and Engineering teams, turning what you see in customer security programs into product feedback.

  • Stay current on frontier LLM capabilities and the new classes of vulnerabilities and attacks they surface
  • Travel occasionally to customer sites for workshops and technical deep dives

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM


The Anduril Government Relations (GR) team is responsible for developing and implementing Anduril’s government affairs strategy with the federal legislative and executive branches as well as state and local government officials.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking talented Government Relations professionals to join the team in Washington, DC. We are actively hiring for multiple roles across several key business lines, each offering unique technology focus areas, as well as Government Relations professionals with significant national security expertise in the legislative or executive branch with experience in budget, authorization, appropriations, and broader national security policy making.

Anduril Government Relations directly supports Anduril’s divisions and associated business lines. This role will be aligned across capability portfolios based on expertise and experience as well as the demands of existing and emerging business lines and capabilities. Specific focus areas include, but are not limited to the below:

  • Maritime: Anduril’s growing maritime business line is building the next generation of autonomous maritime capability. In addition, Anduril recently announced Arsenal-2, a new, software-defined shipyard in Maryland, which will build complex components and large scale assemblies as a supplier in the submarine industrial base.

  • Missiles and Advanced Effects: Anduril’s growing advanced weapons and autonomous effects portfolio. Anduril's Advanced Effects business line develops and manufactures autonomous air vehicles, cruise missiles, interceptor missiles, loitering munitions, and one-way effectors designed to give the U.S. military affordable, high-volume strike options to resolve the critical munitions gap.

  • Space: Anduril’s growing space business line is expanding our AI-powered capabilities our AI-powered capabilities, enhancing space domain awareness, space control, and command and control for national security applications. We're developing fully integrated hardware and software systems to address growing threats in space to maintain a decisive advantage in this contested warfighting domain.

  • Unmanned and Counter Unmanned Systems: Anduril builds a comprehensive, AI-driven suite of Counter-UAS (C-UAS) solutions designed to detect, track, identify, and defeat unmanned aerial threats. In addition, Anduril builds unmanned aerial systems (UAS) ranging from small Group One sized quadcopters to larger UAS systems.

  • Command and Control and Autonomous Systems: Anduril’s Lattice is the software platform that powers the capabilities of its software-defined weapons, and easily integrates with third-party and government-owned capabilities to create a comprehensive, extensible network of sensors and effectors.

In these roles, you will assist in the development of engagement strategies with Members of Congress and their staff, Committee Staff, Congressional Leadership teams, Caucuses and other bodies, as well as the executive branch in connection with. You will also represent the company before a range of audiences to include Members of Congress and their staff, Committee Staff, executive branch officials, industry groups, and other audiences as appropriate.

You must have significant knowledge and experience of the national security related US federal budget/appropriations and policymaking processes and how these processes impact and support the company’s business development agenda. You should be a self-starter with strong verbal and written communication skills, and work well as part of a team. If you take initiative and find innovative solutions to drive forward priorities in a dynamic, fast paced team-oriented environment, this might be the job for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO


As a key Member of the Government Relations team, roles and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

  • Support the development and execution of near term and long term government relations strategies to build the company’s reputation, enhance the strategic positioning in the industry, and increase the understanding of the company and its business objectives in Washington, DC.

  • Develop and implement GR strategy across business lines and fiscal years and engage on company-wide efforts to enact strategic national security policy and funding priorities through the congressional and executive branch processes.

  • Support the planning and execution of appropriations and authorization strategies leading to direct revenue capture for multiple business lines, to include the engagement strategy with Members of Congress and their staff, Congressional Leadership teams, Caucuses and other bodies to increase support for budgetary and policy requests that have direct and material impact on Anduril revenue targets.

  • Coordinate and oversee visits by congressional Members and staff to Anduril facilities in the United States and, as required, internationally.

  • Support the company’s congressional engagement process to include the drafting and submission of policy and funding requests and supporting documentation, white papers, power points, congressional testimony and hearing prep, and other required deliverables.

  • Monitor, analyze, and engage the annual congressional policymaking process to support the company’s priorities with a particular focus on annual appropriations, and defense and homeland security policy.

  • Collaborate internally and externally on Anduril priorities, messaging and general outreach to ensure coordination and integration across the business development teams, independent consultants and senior leadership at the company.

  • Support the company’s Political Action Committee priorities.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • At least 6+ years of experience in the national security, government relations, and/or federal executive or legislative arena is recommended. Title and Salary will be commensurate with experience.

  • Holds considerable defense/national security experience on Capitol Hill or government relations related positions either for the Executive Branch or in a similar defense industry position.

  • Demonstrated success in planning and implementing strategies to promote government relations priorities and influence change in the legislative policy and budget process.

  • Significant knowledge and understanding of US federal appropriations and policy making processes, including executive agencies, the White House, Senate and House and an understanding of how these processes impact the company’s business development agenda.

  • Experience with defense policy and budget issues and knowledge of the defense and national security sector and key stakeholders.

  • Ability to build coalitions and to develop and maintain relationships with key Congressional and executive branch officials and industry and trade associations.

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.

  • Proven ability to work independently to pursue short and long-term goals.

  • The ability to work and be an integral part of an action-oriented, decision-making working environment.

  • Bachelors degree required. Graduate degrees welcome but not required.

  • Ability to travel approximately 25% or greater.

  • Must be available to work on-site in our DC Office

  • Position will require individual lobbyist registration under the Lobbying Disclosure Act of 1995.

  • Currently possesses or is eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates.     • Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

  • What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

About the Team

Anduril's Air Defense team builds robots that find other robots and knock them out of the sky. At a time when air superiority can no longer be taken for granted, we provide mission critical capabilities to warfighters. From detection to tracking, identification, deterrence, and defeat, our family of networked sensors and effectors enables our customers to rapidly close the kill chain against a broad range of UAS threats. Working across product, engineering, sales, logistics, operations, and mission success, the Air Defense team develops, tests, deploys, trains, and sustains our Family of Systems (FoS) in challenging operational environments worldwide.

About the Job

As a Deployment and Training Lead on the Air Defense team, you are responsible for delivering, training, and sustaining a capability that meets our customers' mission requirements and exceeds their expectations. You own the full lifecycle of a deployment — from planning and installation through training, sustainment, and continuous improvement. You fulfill this responsibility through rigorous operational planning, execution, detail orientation, proactive communication, deep mission understanding, and hard-won product expertise.
You feel ownership over the health and performance of all assets and technologies deployed to your customers and users, and ensure that the system delivers when they need it most. You are equally invested in ensuring that end users are trained, confident, and proficient in employing the capability. You develop and deliver world-class training programs, identify knowledge gaps, and build solutions that drive user proficiency and operational readiness.
You represent Anduril to our customers, building their confidence and trust through your professionalism and commitment to excellence. You also represent our customers back to Anduril, communicating user feedback and lessons learned to continuously improve our products, curriculum, and our team in response to evolving mission needs. Above all, you set the standard for what good looks like for your deployment, and you rally your Anduril teammates to meet that standard every single day.
In this role, you will manage deployments of Anduril's Air Defense products while ensuring mission readiness to support national security infrastructure. Collaborating closely with the Program Manager and Program Chief Engineer, you will play a crucial role in developing long-term deployment, training, and sustainment operations aligned with customer priorities. As a key team member, you will engage across multiple business lines and facilitate customer interactions, making flexibility, humility, and a collaborative mindset - essential qualities for success.

What You'll Do

  • Deployment planning and execution: We execute hundreds of deployment events each year, including site installations, test and evaluation exercises, demonstrations, training events, and maintenance visits. You will orchestrate these events, leading a cross-functional team that spans hardware supply, logistics, engineering, and more to do whatever it takes to achieve mission success for Anduril and our customers. Meticulous, resourceful, and detail-oriented, you will manage every step of the deployment process, from site survey to testing, pack-out, installation, training, and sustainment. No job is too small. You consistently demonstrate extraordinary judgment, grit, and composure in high-pressure situations. You anticipate every contingency, build lightweight processes, soberly assess and mitigate risk, and deliberately learn from your experiences to continuously improve.
  • Training development and delivery: You own the training mission for your deployments. You develop and deliver training curricula across a variety of formats — from computer-based simulations and knowledge portals to hands-on individual and collective training events. You create and maintain training materials that keep pace with evolving product capabilities. You identify knowledge gaps and training opportunities, plan and resource realistic training events, and ensure end users are proficient and confident in employing the full Family of Systems. You are passionate about educating others on groundbreaking technology and measure your success by the operational readiness of the forces you support.
  • Relationship management: Build trust with customers, industry partners, users, and Anduril teammates through effective communication, positive attitude, and follow-through. With careful listening and observation, you internalize your counterpart's priorities and requirements. With empathy and responsiveness, you quickly build rapport, trust, and confidence in our capability. You develop relationships across the organization and communicate honestly and directly. You are committed to giving and receiving feedback well. Your partners always know what you expect from them, and know exactly what to expect from you.
  • Mission expertise: Develop a deep knowledge of your customer's mission requirements, including the nature of the threats they face, regulatory challenges, resource constraints, rules of engagement, and more. You will become a subject matter expert and the voice of the customer, capable of effectively communicating requirements and CONOPS to Anduril engineers so they can continue to enhance our capability to meet evolving mission needs. You serve as the counter unmanned systems (cUAS) subject matter expert for your customers, helping them resource realistic training and manage all hardware and software configurations for cUAS-peculiar equipment. You are deeply motivated to shape the future of air defense.
  • Product expertise: Develop a thorough understanding of the capabilities and limitations of Anduril's Family of Systems. You are innately curious about the technology underpinning our capability, and are not satisfied with a superficial understanding of how and why it works. You are constantly educating yourself about the strengths and weaknesses of different sensor modalities, the challenges of sensor fusion, power and networking requirements, and more. You will become an opinionated power user who can reliably forecast how our capability will perform against a broad range of threat profiles, environmental conditions, and mission constraints.
  • Hardware and software configuration management: Manage the end-to-end hardware and software configurations for all assigned equipment at your deployment sites. You ensure systems are properly configured, updated, and maintained to deliver peak performance.

Required Qualifications

  • Advanced degree or 5+ years of experience in a technical field, preferably in the defense, national security, or aerospace domain
  • Proven experience developing and administering technical training,
  • Highly organized creative problem-solver with proven project management skills
  • Experienced in the creation and upkeep of documentation for new or developing processes, including training curricula and programs of instruction
  • Proven experience leading tech-enabled teams of peers while building a culture of influence through relationships
  • Deep interest in national security issues and defense technologies, with a commitment to lifelong learning
  • Experience translating technical concepts into operational requirements, performance specifications, and training materials
  • Ownership mentality with strong initiative in managing your own work in isolated or remote environments
  • Comfort communicating complex concepts simply across various methods of communication and tools
  • Ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and prioritize tasks effectively
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance; Top Secret preferred
  • Experience in field operations
  • Willing to travel up to 60% of the time

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior military experience, particularly in Air Defense, Fires, or related operational roles
  • Operational experience delivering defense technology solutions to USG customers in operational environments
  • Active U.S. Top Secret security clearance

ABOUT THE TEAM

Production technology (ProdTech) is a organization that enables Anduril’s end to end production processes through technology, drives adoption/adherence, and determines the roadmap of our production enterprise systems.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

Team Development and Resource Planning

  • Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing team of individuals responsible for the training and adoption of new systems
  • Foster cross-functional collaboration across engineering teams.
  • Promote a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Manage budgets, resources, and staffing.

Process Development & Operational Execution:

  • Establish and own the end-to-end support model (Tier 1/2/3 escalation paths, triage workflows, and on-call rotations) for mission-critical enterprise systems.
  • Define and track operational SLAs (First Response Time, Time to Resolution, System Availability) to prevent operational bottlenecks on the production floor.
  • Build robust feedback loops with core Engineering and Product teams, translating frontline tickets and system bugs into prioritized roadmap features.

Training, Enablement & Change Management:

  • Architect comprehensive, role-based training programs and certifications for shop-floor operators, manufacturing engineers, and supply chain teams.
  • Design and execute change management plans for new system rollouts, migrations, and major software releases, minimizing operational disruption.
  • Implement modern learning tools, digital adoption platforms, and dynamic documentation that keep pace with rapid, continuous software deployment.

Cross-Functional Collaboration:

  • Partner deeply with Factory Operations, Quality, Central IT, and Software Engineering to align tooling with real-world operational workflows.
  • Serve as the executive escalation point for production-blocking software issues.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years in software, systems, or manufacturing engineering, including 3+ years leading engineering teams, with experience managing managers or a clear readiness to.
  • Demonstrated ownership of enterprise production systems at scale — MES, ERP, MRP, WMS, PLM, or equivalent — including the integration layer between them.

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Air Dominance and Strike MRB Mechanical Engineering Team supports the production, sustainment, and airworthiness of Group 5 air vehicles and missile platforms. The team is focused on keeping fielded and in-production systems flying — evaluating nonconforming hardware, driving Material Review Board (MRB) dispositions, resolving production issues, and ensuring mechanical subsystems meet performance and safety requirements throughout their operational lifecycle. The team works at the intersection of engineering, manufacturing, and quality to maintain the pace of production without compromising airworthiness.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Coordinate with the manufacturing and engineering teams for all of Mechanical Subsystems, including: propulsion, hydraulic systems, fuel systems, landing gear, and systems integration
  • Evaluate nonconforming mechanical hardware and components on fielded and in-production Group 5 air vehicles, and determine engineering dispositions that restore airworthiness and function
  • Generate clear, traceable MRB dispositions — including rework instructions and repair solutions — for mechanical subsystems, actuation, and structural-mechanical interfaces
  • Review and interpret CAD models, 2D drawings, GD&T, and tolerance stack-ups to assess fit, function, and manufacturability impacts of non-conformances
  • Identify acceptable alternate components for obsolete parts
  • Perform structural and mechanical analysis (stress, deflection, fatigue) using hand calculations and FEA tools to substantiate dispositions and repairs
  • Lead root cause analysis and corrective action efforts for recurring non-conformances and production escapes on mechanical hardware
  • Partner daily with Manufacturing, Quality, Design Engineering, and Supply Chain to resolve build issues and keep production flowing without compromising safety or performance
  • Build prototypes and test fixtures in the field or on the production floor; analyze failures and feed learnings back into design
  • Travel to vendor, production, and test sites as needed to support hardware builds and troubleshoot issues directly
  • Provide technical guidance and mentorship to junior engineers on MRB discipline, mechanical fundamentals, and cross-functional coordination

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • B.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or equivalent experience
  • 5+ years of mechanical engineering experience, including direct experience evaluating nonconformances and dispositioning hardware in a production, depot, or maintenance environment
  • Proficiency with 3D CAD tools (CATIA, Siemens NX, Creo, or SolidWorks) and strong command of GD&T and tolerance stack-up analysis
  • Ability to perform structural and mechanical analysis (stress, deflection, fatigue) using hand calculations and FEA tools (ANSYS, NASTRAN, or equivalent)
  • Understanding of manufacturing methods relevant to mechanical hardware (machining, sheet metal, fasteners, actuation, 3D printing)
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills — able to produce clear, technically sound disposition and repair documentation under schedule pressure
  • Self-driven with strong autonomy and adaptability in a fast-paced, dynamic environment
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct MRB signature/delegated authority on a production aerospace program
  • Experience with Siemens NX/Teamcenter or other PLM systems
  • Experience integrating electrical and mechanical subsystems into advanced air vehicles
  • Familiarity with military airworthiness and certification processes (Military Commercial Derivative Aircraft certification, FAA STC, Military Airworthiness Certification)
  • Experience with FMEA and other risk assessment methodologies
  • Hands-on experience in an aircraft manufacturing, depot repair, or sustainment environment
  • Broad experience across a range of aircraft or missile programs

The Industrial Security team is a highly specialized security team responsible for managing Anduril’s cleared personnel, classified programs, and secure facilities. We operate at the intersection of cutting-edge defense technology and stringent security requirements, ensuring the integrity and protection of national security. Our team is composed of experts in security management, compliance, risk assessment, and physical security, dedicated to upholding the highest standards of security in support of national and international defense initiatives while providing the best customer service, both within Anduril and externally.

ABOUT THE JOB

Serve as a member of Anduril Industries Security Services Team supporting employees throughout the United States. Work within a collaborative team environment and take independent action, analyze problems, and provide focused solutions to effectively communicate information to various audiences orally and through written communications. Leverage expertise with US government security policies and procedures as it relates to the personnel security program. Maintain responsibility for updates to various databases, security clearance processing, and review documentation for accuracy and completeness. Address personnel security matters and other clearance-related actions for personnel requiring clearances for collateral positions. Interact daily with internal and external clients and government security officials to resolve issues.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Support our Personnel Security Team in accordance with government policies, which has duties as outlined below:
  • Manage and initiate personnel clearances background investigations and process visit access requests (VARs) and mandatory SEAD 3 reporting via Defense Information System for Security (DISS).
  • Process requests for reciprocity from other agencies such as DOE, NSA, CIA, etc.
  • Provide employees with personnel security guidance consistent with the 13 adjudicative guidelines to assist them in managing their clearances.
  • Handle in-person and virtual requests and inquiries, as it pertains to Security Services Help Requests, Security Forms, Incoming/Outgoing Visit Requests, New Hire Orientation Briefings, Cleared Employee Training, Foreign National Contacts and Foreign Travel Briefings.
  • Process visitor requests; enter clearance information into the visitor database and/or research information in DISS and internal clearance database.
  • Coordinate classified meetings requiring VARs; liaison between Security Services and Anduril meeting hosts to facilitate meetings.
  • Additional Duties:
    • Manage the internal security database with clearance, access, visit, and adverse information.
    • Perform citizenship verification and fingerprinting.
    • Communicate with Anduril employees on additional information requests.
    • Enforce Anduril’s security policies and procedures.
    • Update databases for clearance and visitor tracking.
    • Ensure Anduril information in DISS is accurate and timely.
    • Assist the Security Services Team, as needed.
    • Perform other work-related duties as assigned.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • High school diploma and two years of related administrative and customer service experience.
  • Possesses excellent organization and tracking skills, and attention to detail and is comfortable in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience with conducting briefings and debriefings; ability to clearly explain security processes and procedures
  • Experience with DoD 32 CFR Part 117, National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM).
  • Experience with DoD Manual 5105.21 Volumes 1 and 3.
  • Experience with DoD clearance processes such as DISS, NBIS, eAPP, and SF86 (PVQ) is desired.
  • Proficiency in use of computers and Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook).
  • Ability to communicate and interact professionally and courteously both orally and in writing with all levels of employees and guests.
  • Reliable attendance and punctuality is required. Anduril is an “in-person” office.
  • Ability to handle multiple demands and prioritize workload based on urgency.
  • Must hold a current U.S. Secret security clearance.
  • Familiar with DISS.
  • Familiarity with SIMS or other security software.

This Product Manager will serve as the connective tissue between the Voyager product line, the Growth team, internal Anduril stakeholders, and external customer requirements. This role is responsible for owning product direction input and ensuring effective communications across all stakeholders—irrespective of whether the products are first party or third party delivered. While closely collaborating with the First Party team, this position will ensure that product decisions reflect both market intelligence and internal operational needs.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

1. Voyager Product Voice & Input

  • Customer & Internal Feedback: Translate field feedback, customer intelligence, internal demand signals, and operational pain points into actionable product insights.
  • Structured Feedback Loop: Establish regular channels to gather input from internal hardware recipients (e.g., Air Defense, Mission Command, Maritime) and relay it to Voyager product leadership.
  • Product Prioritization: Collaborate with stakeholders to drive alignment on product priorities, including roadmap visibility, EOL planning, and new features (e.g., GPU upgrades, VM4 successors).
  • Representation: Attend and contribute to Voyager product reviews and planning sessions, ensuring every voice—from internal teams to customer-facing groups—is considered.

2. Growth Team Integration

  • Growth Bridge: Act as the primary liaison between the Growth team and the Voyager product line to ensure that external, customer-facing data enhances product decisions.
  • Structured Intakes: Develop and implement predictable processes (e.g., templates, cadences, forums) to capture key customer insights, competitive gaps, capability requests, and deployment challenges. Build off the work Division Operations has already done here (ie Growth Product Roundtables) as well as the weekly Voyager NPI Sales meetings.
  • Upcoming Product Rollouts: Ensure that the Growth team is well-informed of upcoming Voyager product decisions, enabling proactive customer communications.

3. Internal Communications Leadership

  • Product Communication: Own and manage Anduril-internal communications regarding Voyager product updates, changes, and decisions.
  • Central Information Hub: Maintain and evolve the Voyager channel to serve as the source of truth for product announcements, updates, and strategic insights.
  • Regular Updates: Produce periodic updates that detail product changes to keep all relevant teams informed.

4. Cross-Functional Stakeholder Management

  • Relationship Management: Strengthen relationships between Voyager teams (including Dublin counterparts), US-based teams, and external partners.
  • Issue Escalation: Collaborate with the Product Operations team to raise challenges related to quality, and work with Supply Chain to raise issues related to delivery timelines.
  • Operational Alignment: Collaborate with supply chain, demand planning, and manufacturing teams to ensure product decisions are smoothly integrated into operational processes.

5. Division Operations Continuity

  • Collaborative Support: Continue supporting broader operational goals, including demand planning, hardware/software integration, and internal partnership development.
  • Broader Scope: Where applicable, lend expertise to other product lines that overlap with the functionalities of the Voyager platform.

  • 3-5 years in product operations, program management, supply chain coordination, or a similar cross-functional role within a hardware manufacturing environment
  • Demonstrated experience working across manufacturing, supply chain, logistics, and sales functions simultaneously
  • Experience tracking production metrics, inventory positions, or fulfillment timelines
  • Ability to take fragmented signals from multiple functions and assemble them into a clear picture for leadership
  • Prior experience succeeding in influence-based roles driving outcomes through persistence and relationships rather than org chart leverage
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. security clearance
  • Willing to travel as necessary (~10%)

  • Defense or government hardware experience — commercial networking equipment, industrial electronics, or similar physical product lines are relevant
  • Familiarity with ERP systems (SAP), PLM tools, or demand planning processes
  • Knowledge of ITAR/export-controlled supply chains
  • Experience with networking or compute hardware specifically

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maneuver Dominance team is building Thunder - an autonomous attack rotorcraft built to fight alongside crewed combat aviation to deliver overwhelming mass effects deep beyond the front lines.

Autonomy is only as good as the link that carries it. Thunder is a compact airframe with weapons, sensors and radios competing for the same antenna real estate, flying low and in formation, in a spectrum that is actively contested. That is the problem you would own.

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril is seeking a Senior Robotics Software Engineer to join the Thunder Team at our Costa Mesa HQ. In this role, you will be responsible for solving a wide variety of problems involving networking, autonomy, systems integration, robotics, perception, and more, while making pragmatic engineering tradeoffs along the way. Your will ensure that Anduril products seamlessly work together to achieve a variety of critical outcomes. This will require strong systems-level knowledge and experience. If you are someone who possess a “Whatever It Takes” mindset—executing in an expedient, scalable, and pragmatic way while keeping the mission top-of-mind and making sound engineering decisions then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the mission autonomy systems and services that are deployed to customers.
  • Write code to improve products and scale the mission capability to more customers.
  • Collaborate across multiple teams to plan, build, and test complex functionality.
  • Create and analyze metrics that are leveraged for debugging and monitoring.
  • Triage issues, root cause failures, and coordinate next-steps.
  • Partner with end-users to turn needs into features while balancing user experience with engineering constraints.
  • Travel up to 25% of the time to build, test, and deploy capabilities in the real world.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Strong engineering background from industry or school, ideally in areas/fields such as Computer Science, Software Engineering, Mathematics, or Physics
  • 7+ years of professional industry experience working with C++ or Rust programming languages.
  • Experience building software solutions involving significant amounts of data processing and analysis.
  • Ability to quickly understand and navigate complex systems and established code bases.
  • A desire to work on critical software that has a real-world impact.
  • Must be willing to travel up to 25% for testing and demonstrations.
  • Active Secret Clearance Required

PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS

  • Strong background with focus in Physics, Mathematics, and/or Motion Planning to inform modeling & simulation (M&S) and physical systems.
  • Developing and testing multi-agent autonomous systems and deploying in real-world environments.
  • Feature and algorithm development with an understanding of behavior trees.
  • Developing software/hardware for flight systems and safety critical functionality.

Anduril is seeking a Senior Systems Engineer to lead the design, integration, verification, and validation of a specific payload or weapon module for the Thunder platform. Directly lead, or provide technical direction to, a multidisciplinary team of 6 to 8 engineers spanning software, electrical, and mechanical and structural disciplines, and drive hands on technical execution from requirements through test, fielding, and sustainment.This is a high-visibility leadership position that directly dictates how versatile and mission-effective the aircraft platform will be in the field.

  • Experience with weapon and store carriage structural design, including mounting, load analysis, and jettison and separation clearance

About the Program

The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) brings researchers and scientists together to tackle consequential problems in AI. In partnership with Scale Labs, we are building a small cohort of researchers to work on the empirical foundations of AI safety.

That work includes finding where models fail, checking whether safety controls hold up under pressure in realistic settings, and studying how AI agents (mis-)behave over long-horizon tasks. Scholars take open research questions like these and turn them into work that improves how frontier AI systems are evaluated and safeguarded.

Each scholar owns a substantial part of a safety research project. You'll work alongside a mentor from the research question through the experiments to deciding what to test next.

Research Areas

Mentors will guide Research Scholars on projects in selected AI safety research areas in select AI safety research areas, such as:

  • AI control and chain-of-thought monitoring: Developing techniques to oversee and constrain AIs, including detecting harmful intent or deception.
  • Alignment auditing and evaluations: Building scalable methods to test whether models have hidden goals, misaligned behaviors or unsafe tendencies.
  • Multi-agent safety: Studying the risks that emerge when multiple agents interact, such as collusion, coordinated failures, or unexpected collective behavior.
  • Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) safety: Investigating how to keep AI systems safe and aligned as AIs increasingly contribute to their own development.
  • Science of Evaluations: examining when and how models recognize they're being tested, and how situational awareness affects the reliability/validity of evaluations.
  • Misuse risks and evaluations: Developing methods to assess how AI systems could be exploited by malicious actors, including evaluating their potential to enable harmful activities.

Projects are matched to demonstrated expertise; we don’t expect any candidate to cover every area.

Representative Research

  • ASPI: 728 task–attack scenarios testing how clarification-seeking changes prompt-injection vulnerability in LLM agents.
  • PropensityBench: simulating real-world pressure to choose between safe or harmful behavior
  • BioRiskEval: evaluating whether safeguards for open-weight bio-foundation models remain robust under fine-tuning and probing.
  • See more work from the Human Frontier Collective.

What You'll Do

Projects are mentor-guided. By default, you will be given a list of research proposals and match you with one based on your research interests and background. You’ll meet weekly with a Scale researcher who sets the direction and gives feedback, and you will drive the day-to-day work.

  • Own research end to end: Turn a high-level safety question into hypotheses, baselines, and controlled experiments, and produce work that others can inspect and build on.
  • Build the measurement: Implement and debug evaluation harnesses, agent environments, datasets, monitoring methods, or post-training experiments.
  • Exercise research judgment: Identify confounds, separate what a model can do from what it tends to do, make sense of negative results, and decide what to try next without step-by-step direction.
  • Make the work legible: Produce reproducible code, experiment logs, analysis, and precise technical writing. External outputs, where appropriate, remain subject to research, security, and communications review. Outputs also include research papers, which will be submitted to top ML conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR).

Who We're Looking For

You may be a good fit if you:

  • are motivated by reducing catastrophic risks from advanced AI systems;
  • are interested in technical safety research, such as alignment evaluations, AI control, monitoring, multi-agent safety, or open-weight model safety;
  • are pursuing or have completed a PhD in CS, ML, statistics, mathematics, or a related field (we also encourage researchers with an equivalent track record to apply);
  • can make progress with high-level guidance, including implementing, debugging, getting unstuck, interpreting results, and proposing next experiments;
  • communicate research clearly and handle confidential information and internal systems responsibly.

Application Process

  • Apply: Submit your resume or CV, your Google Scholar profile if you have one, and one research project you substantially owned, with 2–3 sentences on your contribution.
  • Research background discussion: Walk us through a past project, including what you tried, what didn't work, and what you learned.
  • Research design: Work through a research problem with us and propose how you'd approach it.
  • Onboarding: Successful candidates complete the applicable recruiting, work-authorization, security, and project-onboarding steps.

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. About the Role

Anthropic's Executive Briefing program brings senior leaders from our most strategic customers together with our spokespeople, product leaders, and researchers. As a Program Manager, Executive Briefings, you will run the program at one of our briefing centers and help build the global operating model that ensures an exceptional and consistent experience across the globe.

You will be the main program lead for your location and own briefings end to end: qualification and intake, agenda design, speaker selection, and day-of execution. You will set the objectives and design for each agenda and develop it jointly with Sales. You will also be the local account teams' go-to partner on how to use a briefing to move their most important opportunities forward.

You will manage the global workstream and set the standard every center follows, so customers get the same quality of briefing wherever they meet us. This is a highly cross-functional role. You will work with regional GTM leadership and the Office of the CCO on account selection and program strategy, with Product Marketing on content, with Solutions on technical deep-dives and demos, with Anthropic's executive bench on sponsorship and participation, and with Workplace, Security, and Revenue Operations on the experience and systems behind every briefing. You will be comfortable running every part of a briefing yourself and maintaining tight alignment with internal stakeholders.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the Executive Briefing program at your location: the local calendar, capacity planning, the request and intake process from Sales, and operating SLAs, applied against global criteria and regional allocation
  • Work with regional GTM leadership to decide which strategic accounts receive a briefing each quarter, hold the qualification bar, and proactively surface accounts that should be engaged
  • Lead discovery with account teams before each briefing to understand the customer's objectives, business context, and stage of evaluation, and turn that into a tailored agenda
  • Own agenda design and co-own agenda development with Sales for every briefing, including the narrative arc, discussion topics, speakers, and demos
  • Build and manage the speaker bench for your location: identify, source, and match speakers to briefings, run prep, and manage capacity so no one is over-asked
  • Own day-of orchestration and the customer experience standard at your center, in partnership with Workplace on logistics
  • Contribute to the playbooks, tooling, and best practices that let the program scale consistently across centers while allowing for regional nuance
  • Share intake and triage on a rotation across time zones so every request gets a decision within the defined SLA
  • Maintain one source of truth for criteria, lead times, and process so account teams get one answer
  • Own measurement and reporting for your center and contribute to global reporting on briefing volume, capacity and allocation, strategic-account coverage, and program-influenced pipeline and expansion
  • Onboard and coach briefing team members and contractors across locations

Minimum qualifications

  • Experience running executive briefings, customer events, or a comparable program for senior external audiences
  • Program management skills, including intake and prioritization, capacity planning, and managing multiple concurrent programs against SLAs
  • Experience designing agendas and facilitating discussions with C-level or other senior customer audiences
  • Experience building processes, playbooks, or tooling that help a program operate consistently
  • Ability to track, report on, and communicate program metrics such as volume, coverage, and pipeline influence
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to partner credibly with field leadership, executives, and internal subject matter experts
  • Work on site at your briefing center when briefings take place

Preferred qualifications

  • 6+ years of experience building or scaling an executive briefing program, or a similar customer-facing program, at an enterprise technology company
  • Experience in a high-volume briefing environment
  • Experience with CRM and reporting tools such as Salesforce, and with connecting program activity to pipeline and expansion outcomes
  • Experience identifying and surfacing speakers for the speaker bench and managing speaker capacity across product, research, and executive teams
  • Experience working across time zones or across multiple sites to set one global standard
  • Experience onboarding or coaching new team members or contractors
  • Familiarity with AI products and how enterprises evaluate and adopt them
  • Interest in Anthropic's mission to build AI that is safe and beneficial

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
